News.title: Builder, 36, died just weeks after scooping £25k jackpot online prize draw – as tributes pour in
News.content:
'LOYAL & GENUINE' Builder, 36, died just weeks after scooping £25k jackpot online prize draw – as tributes pour in

A BUILDER has died just weeks after winning a £25,000 jackpot, prompting heartrending tributes to flood in.

Carl Blakemore, 36, was found dead after winning the prize money from an online competition site just weeks beforehand.



The provisional cause of death was given as hanging, an inquest heard.

Described as a “hardworking and genuine lad” by his colleagues, Carl from Tonyrefail, South Wales, was said to have made a “lasting impact on everyone”.



Carl’s bosses at Davies Contractors Ltd are now urging people to “speak to others” and “break the stigma around men’s mental health“.

The firm said: “Carl wasn’t just an employee – he was part of our family.

“He was a hardworking, loyal, genuine lad who made a lasting impact on everyone who had the privilege of working alongside him.

“His passing has deeply affected every single one of us at Davies.



“It is a reminder that life is precious and that behind every smile, there can be battles that others cannot see.”

They added that mental health can affect people from “all walks of life”, stressing the importance of checking up on friends, family and workmates.

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

“A simple conversation can make all the difference,” they said.

“Rest easy, Carl. You will always be part of the Davies family.”

The construction company held a family fun day in a bid to raise funds for Carl’s grieving family.



The tragic news follows his successful entry in a prize draw run by the online company Vortex.

The site offers participants the chance to win Audi cars, campervans and even £50,000 in cash.

A spokesperson for Vortex shared a tribute to Carl, with the message: “This is Carl. He won £25,000 off us a few weeks ago.”

“Carl sadly passed away last week and I’ve been bombarded with messages telling me the news.”

They added that the company intended to raise money to assist Carl’s family with funeral costs.



A full inquest into his death is due to take place in Pontypridd, South Wales, at a date yet to be confirmed.

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please call the Samaritans for free on 116123.

News.title: Chilling rise of Scandi child soldiers as kids as young as nine are recruited as assassins for ultra-violent cartels
News.content:
BABY-FACED Johannes Natland left his middle-class parents’ comfortable home on the Norwegian coast “to play football with friends” – then the aspiring lawyer disappeared.

A heavy drug user, Natland — who had just turned 18 — told his then-girlfriend: “It will be a bit cool to really kill someone.”



Days later, gun-toting cops ­hammered on the door of a Huddersfield hotel room 500 miles away in West Yorkshire.

In his underwear, Natland emerged and feebly cocked his hands at the armed British police officers to mimic a gun.

But this was no game. Pushing his face into the corridor wall, officers cuffed him and read him his rights.



Under the bed inside the room, they found a 9mm semi-automatic Luger pistol, a revolver, 12 rounds of live ammunition and £2,000 in cash.

On Wednesday an Old Bailey jury found Natland guilty of conspiring to murder an unknown target in the UK. He will be sentenced in October.

This bright and sporty youngster had been recruited online to be a teenage assassin by the Iranian-linked Foxtrot international crime syndicate.

His reward if successful? A blood money bounty of £21,000.

Natland’s mother, journalist Ellen Kongsnes said before her son’s trial that she found the turn of events “completely incomprehensible”.



She added: “It feels like a very bad movie, with a terribly bad script that doesn’t seem realistic at all.”

Yet Natland is one of hundreds of teens recruited across Scandinavia to maim and kill for ultra-violent criminal cartels like Foxtrot.

The Scandi child hoodlums have wreaked carnage in Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and now the UK.

Over a four-month period in 2024 at least 25 Swedish youngsters on suspected contract-killing or bombing missions were arrested in Denmark.



The ground zero for the rise of these child soldiers is Sweden. Long a standard bearer for liberal tolerance, the land of Ikea and ABBA seems from the outside an unlikely haven for teenage assassins.

Yet children as young as 11 have been caught with automatic weapons, while nine-year-old boys act as street-corner lookouts for mobsters.

In one court case it emerged a 15-year-old, who committed murder for around £6,300 in cash, had written to a friend: “I shot I kill.”

The pal’s sickening response was: “Hahahahahaha. Head shot?”



So what attracts Swedish youngsters to the gangster world?

On a visit to capital Stockholm I met 6ft 2in Essa Sallah Kah. Using the street name Big Daddy or The Boss, he once ruled the 150-strong Chosen Ones mob.

Born in violence-ravaged Gambia, West Africa, his family moved to the gang-plagued Rinkeby estate where Essa became mob footsoldier aged just 12.

Powerfully built, he was soon acting as muscle for the area’s Yugoslav and ­Turkish gangs.



He says: “They were drug dealers. They drove nice cars and people had respect for them.

“I wanted to prove that we blacks can do it too. The attitude was, ‘Don’t come and f*** around with us’.”

He began carrying guns — AK-47 assault rifles or Colt handguns — and robbing shops or acting as a menacing debt collector.

Big Daddy then established the Chosen Ones and ­wallowed in the trappings of gangster life.



Driving a Mercedes, he and his retinue of bodyguards secured the best seats in Stockholm’s clubs, adding: “Wherever I went, I had a table. I didn’t stand in queues.” Reaching his 40s, he was a cocaine and amphetamine-addled, 36st mental and physical wreck.

Turning his back on his gangster life and finding God, the 53-year-old — now a social worker — told me: “People saw me as this dangerous guy, but I was anxious inside.

“None of the people who are doing this are happy.”

Yet the cartels — flooding social media with the lure of cash, notoriety and the high life — ­continue to attract wayward youth.



The business model has been compared to the gig economy that employs Uber drivers and Amazon delivery workers.

The gangsters — mostly adults — target children through Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok.

The cash rewards can be irresistible for youngsters living in poverty.

Lobbing a grenade — often used as a crude warning to rival gangsters rather than to kill — is valued at around £4,000, while a murder can earn the perpetrator £12,000.



And it’s not just boys looking for street cred and social media likes — teenage girls in Sweden are touting themselves as hitwomen.

In May, a 12-year-old was convicted after she threw two live hand grenades at a door in Boras, near Gothenburg, last year.

Recruited on social media for cash, she travelled by bus with the devices concealed in her clothing to target relatives of a rival gangland figure.

The grenades failed to detonate. The girl faced no penalty or sentence because she is below 15 — Sweden’s age of criminal responsibility.

Sweden’s Justice minister Gunnar Strommer said: “Girls’ participation in criminal circles is much more widespread than we had previously assumed.”



Stockholm prosecutor Ida Arnell said last year: “I had a case involving a 15-year-old girl recruited to shoot someone in the head.

“She was able to choose the type of mission — to aim at the guy’s door or his head. She chose the head.”

The girl was arrested with a 17-year-old male accomplice, who ended up pulling the trigger. The ­victim was left clinging to life after a shower of bullets lodged in their neck, stomach and legs.



The prosecutor added that girls “have to show that they are even more determined and tougher (than boys) to get the job.” Some 280 ­Swedish girls aged between 15 and 17 were charged with murder, ­manslaughter or other violent crimes in 2024. It is unclear how many were linked to organised crime.

In March, a 15-year-old girl was held in connection with the murder of two teenage boys, one from the southern city of Malmo and the other from the outskirts of Stockholm.

Astonishingly, a new trend shows children not yet in their teens are being recruited by Swedish gangs to conduct violent crime.

Ten children aged seven to 12 were arrested last year on suspicion of ­carrying out violent crimes for gangs.

Many youngsters come from ­Sweden’s immigrant communities. Famed for welcoming asylum seekers from the world’s trouble spots, ­politicians from all parties ­say Sweden has not managed to successfully integrate migrants.



Author and investigative reporter Diamant Salihu, 42, told me: “There’s a consensus now that Sweden has failed with integration.

“Germany has taken in a lot of migrants, but you don’t hear about child soldiers there.”

Much of the rise in Sweden’s teen gangsters traces back to the blood-thirsty cartel Foxtrot, which has links to the Iranian regime.

Its godfather, Rawa Majid, was born in Iran to Kurdish Iraqi parents before the family moved to Sweden.

Known as the Kurdish Fox, his young footsoldiers specialised in ­contract killings and bombing rivals. In 2023 Majid began a feud with one-time friend Ismail Abdo — nicknamed The Strawberry — who had become leader of rival gang Rumba.



Abdo’s mother was murdered at her home in Uppsala, north of Stockholm, by a 15 and 19-year-old. The violence soon spiralled.

In 2024 a string of attacks against Jewish or Israeli targets occurred.

There was a shooting outside the Israeli embassy in Stockholm. Then two Swedish teenagers aged 16 and 19 were arrested in Denmark after hand grenades were detonated near the Israeli embassy in Copenhagen.

Mossad, the Israeli intelligence agency, alleged Majid was working with Iran and blamed both Foxtrot and Rumba for the attacks.

It was Foxtrot that later enticed Norwegian Natland. Recruited by a teen known by the internet alias UnknownHustler, the lad from ­Stavanger was sent a blunt tender for a prospective assassination.



On 15 March 2025, UnknownHustler forwarded him a message reading: “Killing in England 270k (270,000 Norwegian Kroner is about £21,000).

“Have transport ready out of the country. Will smuggle assassin out of the country.

“The police will be paid to look the other way. Nothing can go wrong.”

Natland was then added to a chat group that included a Stavanger-based recruiter named Generalen and another nicknamed Agent 47.

Agent 47 was Ali Shehab, a 22-year-old Swedish-Iraqi gangster and a senior recruiter for Foxtrot.



Natland’s first message to the group — named Assassin EU — was, “Who is to be killed?”

It’s unclear if he was ever told the answer. Just two days later, Natland flew on a one-way ticket from Stavanger to Manchester.

Taking a taxi to Huddersfield, his handlers directed him to where cash and firearms were concealed under rubbish and in woodland.

Paying cash for a room in the Briar Court Hotel, he sent friends videos of himself with the guns.

As the minutes ticked by before the hit, recruiter Generalen was arrested at Oslo airport. Cops found messages about a planned “assassination” in England on his phone.



At 5:15am on March 19 last year cops raided Room 207 at the Briar Court Hotel. Marching out, the green dots from the officers’ guns shone on Natland’s chest.

Foxtrot’s teenage hitman had been stopped. Yet there are seemingly many more ready to take his place.

News.title: Andy Burnham hints at North Sea oil U-turn as he tells Trump he won’t ignore energy reserves
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has told Donald Trump he would not ignore the oil and gas in the North Sea while people are struggling with energy bills.

The Prime Minister said that he had reassured the US President he would take a “pragmatic approach” to drilling.



Mr Trump has long been lobbying for Britain to ramp up North Sea exploration and has railed against wind turbines.

Labour made an election commitment to ban any new drilling licences from being issued as part of Ed Miliband’s Net Zero drive.



But it is thought Mr Burnham, who moved Mr Miliband to the Foreign Office, could be more willing to exploit the energy in the North Sea.

On a visit to Cumbria on Thursday, the PM said: “I indicated in the phone call that we had a week last Monday that I would take a pragmatic approach when it comes to the North Sea, and that is my intention as we go forward from here.



“There is a resource there. When people are struggling, we can’t ignore that.”

There had been confusion on Mr Burnham’s first day in office earlier this month when Mr Trump said he would be “opening up, all the way” North Sea oil reserves.

But deputy Labour leader Lucy Powell said the manifesto commitment to ban new licences would stay in place.

A possible compromise could be to give the go-ahead to the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas fields that are awaiting decisions.



Both have already been granted licences but need approval from new Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has demanded Mr Burnham make the decisions without delay and expand drilling in the North Sea.

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said doing it “would be the first step towards ending Labour’s Net Zero madness that is driving up costs for families and businesses and holding our economy back”.

News.title: Greek cops rush to find CCTV after pinpointing when Brit’s body found in suitcase was placed in abandoned building
News.content:
GREEK cops are rushing to find CCTV of the abandoned building where a Brit woman was found stuffed in a suitcase as they close in on a timeline.

Elisabeth Ross, 38, was last seen leaving a friend’s house in Athens before her dead body was found 72 hours later.



The homeless man who made the grim discovery on July 18 has insisted that the suitcase was not in the building the two days prior.

His testimony has led police to believe her body was taken to the building at 7 Evelpidon Street on the evening of July 17 or the following morning.



They are now combing the area for security cameras that might have captured the suitcase dump.

Local hotels and residences are also being examined, with police speculating that the body was likely taken to the building from close quarters.



Elisabeth arrived in Athens on a flight from Edinburgh on June 26.

She is said to have stayed at a friend’s house in Attica before leaving on July 15 with plans to meet American pals in Kypseli.



But her body was found at the abandoned building three days later, with no visible wounds on the body or any clear signs of a struggle.

Police quickly opened a murder investigation fearing a killer may be on the loose.

Cops are desperate to uncover what happened to Elisabeth during the three days she is unaccounted for – with the homeless man’s testimony giving them a strong lead.



Police spokesperson Konstantia Dimoglidou told The Sun: “The key to this case is to find out what happened to the woman during those three days as we don’t know anything about her moves on the 15th, 16th and 17th.

“The main focus is to find her cause of death as the medical examiner did not find any signs of struggle or injury on her body.

“We are waiting for the toxicology reports to shed some light in the next few days.

“We cannot be talking about a murder if we don’t know what happened to her – maybe she died and someone tried to hide her body, anything is possible and at this point it’s too soon to tell.

“As part of the investigation we are also checking CCTV from the area where she was found and we are working to trace her phone.”



The exact date she died is still unknown, but the toxicology tests will help determine if foul play was involved.

A spokesperson for Greek police said: “No other evidence has emerged from the body or the suitcase that would allow us to identify another person.

“We are awaiting the result of toxicology tests to determine the cause of death, and ascertain whether foul play was involved.

“The investigation is ongoing.”

Cops are also reportedly still probing a theory that Elisabeth may have been lured to the abandoned location by a homeless person.



Officials are also still trying to pin down the route Elisabeth took to get into Kypseli and are quizzing local hotels and bars to see if they recognise her.

The friends who hosted the Scottish woman during her holiday have also been questioned and confirmed she left under her own power and appeared to be in good spirits.

It comes as her heartbroken dad revealed he had received haunting text messages from his daughter’s phone after her mysterious death.

The dad, a lawyer in Edinburgh, told Greek cops he was sent several messages for two weeks after Elisabeth’s passing from a man now being viewed as the prime suspect.

An officer told the Sun that the emergence of the messages has helped investigators track the location of phone.



They said: “They were sent from Athens and it is clear whoever sent them was trying to buy time.”

Elisabeth’s phone was only turned off on Wednesday morning after reports of the body being found made global headlines, local media claim.

First Minister John Swinney said Ross’s family would be supported by the Scottish government and the Foreign and Commonwealth Office.

He said: “This is an absolutely appalling case that has been reported overnight.

“And obviously I’m deeply concerned that such a tragedy has taken place.”

News.title: France faces calls to refund cash UK paid to stop migrants after cops waved small boat migrants through on beaches
News.content:
FRANCE last night faced calls to refund cash paid by the UK to stop the boats as four more migrants died trying to cross the Channel.

Politicians branded the funding deal a “waste of money” after the Home Office said yesterday that 752 migrants reached Britain on Wednesday — the most in a day this year.



It came as three women died of suspected heart attacks on a crowded migrant dinghy which set off from Dunkirk at 6am yesterday.

A French search and rescue team removed the bodies and the boat carried on until a Border Force vessel picked up the others on board.



Just hours earlier another migrant, believed to be in his 30s, died as more than 100 people tried to board an inflatable dinghy off Neufchâtel Hardelot, south of Boulogne.

Six others were seriously injured, including a one-year-old baby who rescuers said “almost drowned”.

The Sun watched repeated launch attempts from beaches including Wimereux and Hardelot where we saw around 60 migrants fighting on a boat stranded just offshore.

Others, at least one holding a baby, were trying to push it back into deeper water during the melee.

Around a dozen French gendarmes stood and watched the disorder.

Reform’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: “The French authorities are waving individuals on to the boats. Enough is enough.



“We should not be sending any more money to France. We have already said that we wouldn’t just end this arrangement, we’d seek a rebate from the French because we’re clearly being taken for fools.”

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp, who was at the beach, added: “The Belgians successfully and safely intervene to stop crossings in exactly the same circumstances. The French should too — and if they refuse then Andy Burnham should stop paying any more money. This will be an early test of his leadership.”

It came after we questioned on our front page yesterday how the PM could claim Labour’s plan to block illegal migration was “working”.



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has signed a £662million agreement with France running until 2029 to tackle Channel crossings.

Around £160million will be paid only if crossings fall.

The rest will go towards drones, helicopters and almost 1,100 police, intelligence and military officers along the north coast of France.

A Home Office spokesman claimed Ms Mahmood’s new payments-by- results deal with France would boost enforcement action on beaches and put people-smugglers behind bars.

He said: “It builds on joint work that’s stopped over 46,000 attempted crossings since the election.”

News.title: Aircraft engineer died after explosion inside fuel tank wearing breathing mask as pals desperately tried to save him
News.content:
PLANE BLAST Aircraft engineer died after explosion inside fuel tank wearing breathing mask as pals desperately tried to save him

A YOUNG aircraft engineer died of a traumatic brain injury after an explosion as he worked inside a plane fuel tank, an inquest heard.

Georgie Buxton, 23, suffered catastrophic injuries after being crushed in the horrifying accident while he was working on a Virgin Atlantic Boeing 787-900.



He underwent several operations after the blast but tragically died in hospital almost a month later.

Now an inquest has heard cops have launched a criminal investigation into the fatal incident alongside the Health and Safety Executive.



Senior coroner Lydia Brown opened and immediately suspended the inquest at West London Coroners’ Court on Thursday.

The hearing was told Mr Buxton was working with another Virgin Atlantic aircraft technician on June 11 at around 8.45am.

The pair had been examining a fuel leak on the aircraft.

Both engineers were wearing breathing apparatus to protect them from residual fuel fumes while inside the tank.

Three colleagues were supporting the operation from outside.

An Aviation Policing spokesman told the court: “Both technicians wore breathing apparatus to protect them from any residual fuel fumes whilst inside the fuel tank.



“They were supported by three colleagues during that task.”

The court heard there was then “a non-combustion explosion” while Mr Buxton was inside the fuel tank.

The spokesman said: “Georgie Buxton took the impact of that explosion to his head and torso causing him to lose consciousness and suffer catastrophic injury.”

His colleague, who was in another part of the fuel tank, escaped unhurt.

The technician managed to move Mr Buxton out of the tank and on to the platform stairs.



The spokesman added: “The bang caused by the explosion was heard by others. The alarm was raised and first aid commenced.”

The London Ambulance Service, Aviation Policing officers and the Helicopter Emergency Medical Service all rushed to the scene.

Mr Buxton was taken to hospital, where he underwent several operations to his head and neck – he died on July 7.

A forensic post mortem examination found he had suffered a traumatic brain injury caused by craniofacial trauma.

The court heard Mr Buxton worked as an aircraft technician for Virgin Atlantic at Heathrow and had previously held the same role with Ryanair.



Police confirmed a criminal investigation is under way.

The Aviation Policing spokesman described the probe as being at “a very early stage” and looking into “very serious and complex matters”.

Coroner Lydia Brown said she was suspending the inquest while detectives continued their investigation and until it becomes clear whether any criminal charges will be brought.

Addressing Mr Buxton’s family and partner, who attended the hearing remotely, she said: “My role as a coroner at this stage is quite a limited one.

“I will, of course, defer to the police investigation. I will simply suspend my inquiry pending the outcome of that.”



She added: “I am going to formally suspend this matter.

“Given I do not know the nature of any potential matters that the police are investigating, and quite rightly so at this stage, I am just going to suspend (the inquest) under my general discretionary powers to do so.”

In a personal message to Mr Buxton’s loved ones, the coroner said: “Can I take this opportunity to say how very sorry I was to learn of the circumstances of this young man’s death.

“Words just can’t explain how difficult this must be for you, please take our sincere condolences this end.
