Sports.title: Senne Lammens cuts short his holiday after World Cup to rejoin Manchester United training - as new signing Youri Tielemans arrives at Carrington
Sports.content:
Senne Lammens cut short his holiday to return early to pre-season training with Manchester United ahead of the new campaign.

The goalkeeper had been due to report back to Carrington next Monday following his participation in the World Cup with Belgium, according to ESPN.

Lammens had been part of the Belgium squad that reached the quarter-finals, before falling to a 2-1 defeat by eventual winners Spain.

The 24-year-old had been Belgium's second choice goalkeeper behind established No1 Thibaut Courtois.

Lammens was called into action in the quarter-final after Courtois sustained an injury, with the Real Madrid shot stopper forced to be substituted.

Lammens was ultimately at fault for Spain's winning goal, with the goalkeeper spilling a shot from distance into the path of Mikel Merino, who scored on the rebound to send Spain into the last four.

Senne Lammens cut short his post World Cup holiday to join Man United's pre-season training

Lammens was expected to report back next week after his World Cup involvement with Belgium

New signing Youri Tielemans was also pictured at Carrington after joining from Aston Villa

Lammens was pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday, four days before he was due to report back to United.

The goalkeeper arrived alongside his international team-mate Youri Tielemans, who signed for United from Aston Villa in a £35million move earlier this month.

ESPN reported that Lammens has been keen to get back to club football following the World Cup.

Lammens had enjoyed a superb debut season at Man United after signing from Royal Antwerp in an £18.2m move last September.

After joining in a deadline day move, Lammens made his United debut in October in a 2-0 win over Sunderland.

Lammens remained an ever present in goal for the remainder of the season, with the goalkeeper playing a key role in helping the Red Devils qualify for the Champions League.

He was voted as the Premier League's transfer of the season in May following an online poll of fans.

Lammens made his international debut for Belgium last November, with his impressive form for United contributing to him being named in their World Cup squad.

United are next in pre-season action on Saturday when Michael Carrick's side face Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

Sports.title: Chaos at the Commonwealth Games as HUGE crash in wheelchair race forces organisers to order a re-run as England star is left 'traumatised' at thought of losing medal
Sports.content:
England’s Ellis Kottas was left ‘lowkey traumatised’ at the prospect of losing her silver medal after Commonwealth chiefs ordered a re-race following a mass wheelchair crash.

Four out of seven athletes finished women’s T54 1500m final on Wednesday night after four crashes, three overturned wheelchairs and a disqualification.

Scotland’s Melanie Woods finished first with Commonwealth record of 3min 33.39sec but the athletes were told the following morning that they must race again.

Kottas said: ‘While I’m lowkey traumatised if I’m going to medal I want to do so on my own merit, so I will go out and give it all I’ve got. If I don’t medal so be it, I’ll still have the incredible memories of lifting that England flag.'

The decision was criticised by Team England’s chef de mission, Jonny Riall, who said: ‘We are incredibly disappointed by the late decision. While there is no formal protest process available to us, we have strongly challenged the decision.

A huge crash out on the first bend of the women's 1500m T54 final 😬 pic.twitter.com/wWNxhKIGqb — TNT Sports (@tntsports) July 29, 2026

Four out of seven athletes finished women’s T54 1500m final on Wednesday night after four crashes, three overturned wheelchairs and a disqualification

'While I really don’t want to rerun the race (lowkey traumatised) if I’m going to medal I want to do so on my own merit,' silver medallist Ellis Kottas said

'The race officials did not halt the race at the time of the incident, nor was any immediate decision made to declare the race void or order a rerun.

'Our priority is the welfare of our athletes. We will now do everything we can do support Ellis during the extremely short turnaround.'

Compliments to the chef as Emily reigns supreme

Not since the Finnieston Crane was in action have Glasgow’s docklands witnessed such large masses of metal being thrown around.

Emily Campbell, with lions weaved into her red and white hair, shifted 278kg – 115 in the Snatch and 163 in the Clean and Jerk – to win gold with a record Commonwealth lift.

On the banks of the River Clyde, England’s Olympian showed her adoring fans why she is regarded as the sport’s great entertainer.

She blew kisses to the crowd and told her rivals that there is ‘life in this old bird yet’ before collecting her medal from the Duchess of Edinburgh.

It takes thousands of calories to fuel a weightlifter and next month Campbell will continue to fly the flag for her sport when the takes part in Celebrity MasterChef.

‘MasterChef is definitely more nerve-racking!’ she laughed.

Emily Campbell, with lions weaved into her red and white hair, shifted 278kg – 115 in the Snatch and 163 in the Clean and Jerk – to win gold with a record Commonwealth lift

‘It’s really nice for me to do something without being Emily the weightlifter, to just do something as Emily. My signature dish is Caribbean and that’s all I’m going to give you because I want you to watch it! It’s another platform to put weightlifting in, another time for us to have that spotlight on us.

At 32, the weightlifting game is beginning taking its toll on her joints. Olympic gold still eludes her but she is yet to commit to competing at LA 2028.

‘We’ve got to look at the practicalities of LA,’ she said. ‘We have to do a slightly different qualification process to other sports. We’ve got to look at that and we can get our body through.

'If I go to LA, I would want to be in contention for a medal, so we want to make sure that that’s feasible. We just have to be very sensible about decisions and hopefully you’ll see me there.

'But for now, we enjoy what happened. We have some good food, maybe a few drinks. We're out in Glasgow!'

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sends emotional message to Barcelona fans ahead of expected return to Manchester United - after Spanish giants rejected chance to sign him for £26m
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford sends emotional message to Barcelona fans ahead of expected return to Manchester United - after Spanish giants rejected chance to sign him for £26m

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message to Barcelona as the countdown continues towards his return to Manchester United.

Rashford spent last season on loan at the Nou Camp, contributing 14 goals and 14 assists as the Catalans won La Liga and reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League.

However, Barca decided not to trigger an option to buy him from United for £26million before a deadline in mid-June, and signed Newcastle’s Anthony Gordon for £70m.

On Thursday, Rashford posted a picture on social media of his No.14 shirt and another of him in action for the club with the message: ‘I am extremely grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here a positive and unforgettable experience. I enjoyed every moment, and I will keep many special memories. I wish the club and all its fans every success in the coming season. Visca Barca!’

Rashford is now set to rejoin United where he has a contract until June 2028 worth around £315,000-a-week. The England international is having some time off after helping England reach the World Cup semi-finals, and it remains to be seen if he will be involved in United’s training camp in Ireland next month which includes a friendly against Leeds at Croke Park on August 12.

With United in need of a left-sided attacker, and Rashford contracted to his boyhood club for another two seasons, it makes sense for the 28-year-old to come back and play under head coach Michael Carrick.

Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message following his season long loan at Barcelona

It is looking increasingly like Rashford will be at Man United when the transfer window closes

There is no chance of a repeat of last summer when the more confrontational Ruben Amorim placed him in a ‘bomb squad’ of five players who trained separately from the main group at Carrington before Rashford left for Barcelona.

After initially putting a price of £40m on their top-earner this summer in the hope of moving him off the wage bill, it has been difficult for United to find a club willing to pay more than the £26m stipulated in the Barca loan as well as Rashford’s salary.

The club also discovered the high cost of replacing him when one option, West Ham’s Crysencio Summerville, joined Al-Hilal for £60m.

There is still time for some twists and turns before the window closes on September 1, but it’s looking increasingly likely that Rashford will be at United when it does.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's solution to Liverpool's defensive crisis: New Reds boss reveals he has no choice but to turn to youth and says it will be 'impossible' for Joe Gomez to return in time for new season
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has backed his rookie teenagers to step up and solve a defensive crisis as the Liverpool boss admitted it is ‘impossible’ for Joe Gomez to be fit for the new season.

Captain Virgil van Dijk has begun work back in Liverpool but is not on the pre-season tour, while fellow centre back Jeremy Jacquet is yet to feature and Giovanni Leoni is still in rehabilitation from a cruciate ligament injury.

Gomez limped off in the Reds’ opening friendly in Nashville last week with a muscle injury but Iraola has given his backing to several kids who have ‘surprised’ him with their ability this fortnight.

‘Joe has a muscle injury,’ said Iraola, who was forced to turn to 18-year-old Ifeanyi Ndukwe – who cannot play this season due to work permit issues – and Luke Chambers, a left back who spent last season on loan at Charlton.

‘It was quite clear since he complained straight away so he will be some weeks off. It’s difficult to say – normally one month. If it goes very well, then a little bit less. If it goes bad then a bit more but it’s a muscle injury.

‘It’s not massive. It will be impossible to have him for the start of the season because we are not so far (away) but it shouldn’t be a lot more.

Andoni Iraola has admitted that he has no choice but to turn to youth in Liverpool's current defensive crisis

Joe Gomez (pictured) picked up an injury in pre-season and Virgil van Dijk is currently the only fit senior centre back at the club

‘You’ve seen in these games that we are pretty thin in the centre back position. We still don’t have Virgil. The only centre-backs we have right now are Mor (Talla Ndiaye) and Ifeanyi who are 18, just arrived at the club and are doing incredibly well.

‘But I’m happy that playing against Sunderland and Wrexham with 18-year-old centre backs, the team has shown composure and solidity at the back and it speaks very well about them.

‘A lot of players have surprised me, especially the young players I did not know before. They have given a very, very high level in these friendlies. They have to grow, which is very good. We will recover players.

‘We have done a great job with these players the first two weeks then we have to integrate the new ones slowly. These players know where we are going and can help us.’

Iraola also said he wants all of his wingers to be able to play on both sides amid talk that every wide forward at the club prefers being on the left, especially with Paris Saint-Germain’s £140million-rated left-winger Bradley Barcola their top target.

Dominik Szoboszlai has been very complimentary about Iraola and said: ‘He is very good, the intensity we need is here now. What we have been missing is back, from the coach and players as well. So now we have to put this together with the team we have.’

The Hungarian signed a new five-year contract earlier this month and added: ‘I am very happy (with the new deal). It was a long way until it was over the line. Hopefully I can stay as long as both sides want and win everything that is possible.’

Sports.title: SANDRO TONALI INTERVIEW: Why Tottenham's new £100m man chose Spurs over Man City and the 'mini connection' the star already has with Roberto De Zerbi
Sports.content:
Our interview with Sandro Tonali is over, but as we shake hands, we have a small correction to make with Tottenham Hotspur’s £100million summer signing.

Earlier on in the conversation, Tonali had explained how nice it was that he was now getting to speak in Italian – with his new manager Roberto De Zerbi and his assistants and team-mates such as Guglielmo Vicario and Destiny Udogie – after three years of only using English at Newcastle United.

Except, as those of us from the heart of the North East will tell you, we do not talk in English. We speak Geordie, and to Tonali’s credit, he appreciates the difference. He tells us how he grew to love the locals who supported him around St James’ Park, and explains how he wanted his old club to feel like they were getting their money’s worth once it became clear that he would be leaving this summer.

‘The first thing was to get the best deal for Newcastle,’ Tonali says when discussing his decision to leave his former side managed by Eddie Howe, whose exit from Newcastle was coincidentally revealed on the same day as we spoke in Sydney.

‘I met there some of the best people for football. They love football. They live for football. When I decided to move, I said to my agent and to Ross Wilson (Newcastle’s sporting director) that I wanted the best deal for Newcastle because they deserve everything. This is football. Sometimes you have to understand how everything can change in your life in five minutes.'

Newcastle are in bother this summer. Not only might Bruno Guimaraes follow Tonali and Anthony Gordon out of the door at St James' Park, they have lost Howe now also. Tonali can only speak for himself, and he explains it was simply time for a change after three seasons and speaking with his family.

Sandro Tonali needed only a few minutes to convince him that Tottenham was his ideal Premier League destination

While sitting inside a makeshift boardroom set up inside Tottenham’s team hotel near the Sydney Harbour Bridge, Tonali explains how it was an easy decision to choose Spurs over others interested.

The £100m asking price that Newcastle placed on him influenced his options as he and his family were initially interested in returning to Italy. But they soon realised those in Serie A could not afford his services.

‘We stayed three years in Newcastle and after three years, we spoke all together, me and my family,’ Tonali says. 'It was impossible for the money (to return to Italy). For the salary, you can speak all the time, but if you don’t find the money for the transfer, you don’t have the chance to move.

'England was our solution and we found the best solution in England for me, for my career, for my football, for my happiness, for my family. I spoke with two teams. I understood after 10, 15 minutes that Tottenham would be my next team.’

Manchester City were believed to be the other club in for Tonali, who has won 32 caps for the Italian national team at 26 years old. He is rather liking the Little Italy connection developing within Tottenham now as he tells us: ‘After the last season, I spoke with my wife. We wanted to change our life. Not just for the city. We wanted to change everything. We spoke with two clubs.

‘When we spoke with Tottenham, we decided to sign for this team. They spoke with 100 per cent passion, 100 per cent seriousness. For this city, for my life outside of football for my family, OK, it’s like 10 per cent. Roberto and the director made the difference to the deal.

'I spoke after two minutes with my wife and my family and I said, “Probably it will be one of my best decisions of my career”. She told me, “You have 100 per cent the control over this decision”. I wanted to speak with her because it’s our life.

‘Roberto said the project will be tough but will be perfect for me, for you, for the city, an we can do one of the best seasons because we have big players. We just have to put a lot of work in.’

Alongside Tonali, Spurs have also spent £85m on signing Mateus Fernandes on West Ham, to complete their midfield. On officially being a £100m footballer, Tonali says: ‘You have to understand that this is football. The price is different now to 10 years ago. I know I have a lot of pressure but I know I’m a football player, I know my responsibilities, I know this team, I know the people here. I have to play like I’m a normal player, a normal Tottenham player, with passion, putting my energy in every day. It’s not £1m, £10m, or £100m. You just have to be a passionate player for this gaffer.’

Tonali previously spent a decade in Italy with Brescia, De Zerbi’s hometown. He and the Spurs boss have this ‘mini connection’, as Tonali describes it, and they previously met up there. ‘We spoke about him, about his work, about the passion that he puts into every single moment with the team for this work and I think now, after two weeks, I know everything is real,’ Tonali adds. ‘All gaffers are different. I passed three years with Eddie and he was fantastic, especially for me. But now I’ve found a different gaffer who works a lot on the pitch, a lot with the tactics, a lot with the ball. We love to play with the ball because we are a big team with big players.’

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott opens up on nightmare Aston Villa loan where he was placed into bomb squad by Unai Emery: 'I wouldn't wish that on any player'
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott opens up on nightmare Aston Villa loan where he was placed into bomb squad by Unai Emery: 'I wouldn't wish that on any player'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Harvey Elliott has opened up on his Aston Villa nightmare, saying he wouldn’t wish the tough year he experienced on anyone.

The 23-year-old was on a high last summer after being named player of the tournament as England won the Under-21s European Championship before he signed for Villa on loan with an obligation to buy for £35million.

But things quickly unravelled after when Elliott fell out of favour under new boss Unai Emery and was plunged into the bomb squad given the clause in his deal that the move from Liverpool would become permanent after playing 10 times.

Elliott could not join another club in January as he had already played one league minute for Liverpool before joining on Deadline Day and UEFA rules dictate players can only feature for a maximum of two clubs in one season.

Now the midfielder is back playing with the Reds, his boyhood club, and has spoken publicly for the first time about his lost year.

‘Mentally, it was a very tough one,’ says Elliott, speaking at the Yankee Stadium after featuring in Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham. ‘(Going to Villa) was a learning curve. It was an opportunity for me to experience something new.

‘I don't wish (the situation) upon any other player, because it's not nice at all, but I have no hard feelings. I wish them all the very best. I did really have a lot of love for them. They treated me as one of their own and for that I respect them highly.

Harvey Elliott has revealed the depths of his frustration with his season-long loan to Aston Villa

The academy star fell out of favour with Unai Emery and had little time in his first team

‘But it was tough, mentally and physically. I'm on the other side of it now. I was able to get through it, and achieve something at the end of the season as well (winning a Europa League medal).’

Elliott will be given a chance to impress this pre-season and has played in both wins on this tour of America, where they beat Sunderland in Nashville and Wrexham in New York.

His longer-term future is more uncertain with a second sale highly possible. However, for now, Elliott is keen to take his second chance and win over the trust of new boss Andoni Iraola — who he later described as ‘incredible’ — after former head coach Arne Slot deemed him surplus to requirements.

‘It’s an incredible feeling (to be back),’ he adds. ‘Everyone knows how much I love the club and I've supported them from a very young age, so the feeling never goes of putting a shirt on, representing the club and doing your childhood dream.

‘I wanted a new challenge. I wanted to kind of go and explore something, come out of my comfort zone, I thought personally that would take me on as a player again. Unfortunately, it didn't work out, but the way I see it is, that's last season — now I'm here. It's kind of a second chance, if you want to call it that.

‘Especially with the gaffer coming in. It's another chance to impress and hopefully get in their (good) books. But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best, had a lot of love for them, and they treated me very, very well. Just keep looking forward.

'I'm here now, and I'm trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad.’

‘Since the first day I walked through the door at the AXA (training centre), I had a big beaming smile on my face and, as I've said before about putting the shirt on, I don't want to take these moments for granted.

'Because last season, I thought it was the last opportunity I'd done it. I'm back now. I'm wearing this strip again and putting this shirt on, and I just want to be free, play as much as I can, just enjoy it, because sometimes I don't feel like I do it enough. Playing at Liverpool, there's no better feeling.’

Elliott placed on record that he harboured no ill-feelings to Emery, adding: ‘He explained very, very clearly and a fair few times. The whole club were very apologetic and ultimately, it was a situation that I couldn't control.’

Sports.title: UEFA statement leaves FIFA with 37-day deadline as World Cup hangs in the balance
Sports.content:
UEFA statement leaves FIFA with 37-day deadline as World Cup hangs in the balance

With the football world turning in on itself after Gianni Infantino's controversial grand plan was wholeheartedly rejected by UEFA, a tournament is now at risk of collapsing

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino's grand World Cup plans already have significant opposition (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto)

UEFA's pledge to boycott FIFA tournaments has seemingly put the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup at risk. The governing body of European football released an imposing statement in response to Gianni Infantino's plan.

‌



The president of FIFA recently unearthed plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors, promising to earn more money for each member nation who expresses support for his idea by September 19. This has been pushed back in the strongest possible way by UEFA and the FA, who insisted all of the 55 member nations will boycott all FIFA competitions for as long as this idea is still alive.

‌



It was a firm statement which came after a meeting held by UEFA president Alexander Ceferin. Assuming UEFA is true to its word, it appears the U20 Women's World Cup is at risk of becoming the first FIFA competition to be effected by this civil war.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

On September 5, the competition is set to begin with the final taking place 22 days later. The competition is being held in Poland and will feature 24 teams from all six FIFA confederations. Out of all of the nations in the group, six are from UEFA as Poland, Italy, England, Portugal, France and Spain are all expected to compete in the tournament. The other nations involved are Argentina, Mexico, Benin, Japan, New Zealand, the USA, Brazil, Tanzania, Canada, North Korea, Costa Rica, Colombia, South Korea, Ecuador, Ghana, Nigeria, New Caledonia and China.

At present, it's currently unclear as to what will happen with the competition. UEFA have made it clear they have no intention in representing any of their member nations in FIFA tournaments for as long as this idea is still going. Considering Infantino's hard deadline to express support is September 19, it's possible the boycott could last until then and beyond. The Swiss football figurehead has also claimed his idea only needs support from just over 50 per cent of its members for the idea to run.

‌



With 55 nations expressing their firm opposition to the idea, Infantino has already lost a firm chunk of potential support. However, other Confederations which include CONCACAF (North American nations), CONMEBOL (South American), the CAF (African Confederation) and Oceania are yet to make their feelings known.

What is clear from UEFA's intervention is that they want the idea to be quashed, quickly. In their statement, they wrote: "UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions. UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

View 3 Images The future of the U-20 Women's World Cup is looking uncertain (Image: 2026 FIFA)

‌



"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

‌



"But our opposition goes far beyond process. The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

View 3 Images North Korea go into the competition as the defending champions (Image: AFP or licensors)

"This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

‌



"As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership. Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

"There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments. Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."

Sports.title: Liverpool signed highly-rated teen, 223-goal striker and title winner from PSG
Sports.content:
Liverpool signed highly-rated teen, 223-goal striker and title winner from PSG

Liverpool are continuing their pursuit of one Paris Saint-Germain star this summer

View 4 Images Liverpool have done a few deals with Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain have a long history of getting deals done in the transfer market. And this working relationship could be strengthened if the Reds convince Bradley Barcola to head to Anfield.

‌



The club are set to open talks with PSG over a potential transfer for the winger. Initial talks with Barcola's representatives have prompted Liverpool to formalise their interest with an official approach.

‌



Andoni Iraola has been on the lookout for a wide player since Mohamed Salah's exit. Barcola has been on Liverpool's radar for some time, and the club will hope to make him their third summer signing.

‌



Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet have signed deals at Anfield, but there's certain to be more movement – both incoming and outgoing – before the new season starts. If Barcola does decide to join Liverpool, it wouldn't represent the first time that a transfer between the two clubs has taken place.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football examines some of the previous transfers between the two sides.

‌



Highly-rated teen

David Ngog signed his first professional contract with PSG in 2006 as a highly-rated teenager. Two years later, he arrived at Anfield as a fresh-faced 19-year-old under Rafael Benitez.

The striker would play under three different managers at Liverpool, including Roy Hodgson and Sir Kenny Dalglish. Ngog scored 19 goals and assisted six times across 94 appearances before leaving for Bolton Wanderers in 2011.

View 4 Images David Ngog spent three seasons with the Reds (Image: John Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Despite such a promising start to his career, Ngog really failed to reach the heights his early days promised. He later played for Swansea City, Reims, Panionios, Ross County and Budapest Honved before retiring in Lithuania at the age of 31.

223-goal striker

Nicolas Anelka had already played in the Premier League before joining Liverpool on loan in 2001. The striker left PSG for Arsenal at 17 and made 42 goal contributions from 1997 to 1999.

A move to Real Madrid came next before Anelka returned to France a year later. PSG then loaned the striker to Liverpool in the 2001 January transfer window.

‌



View 4 Images Nicolas Anelka has plenty of experience in the Premier League (Image: Clive Brunskill/ Getty Images)

The France international made 22 appearances for the Reds and scored five goals, helping the team to a second-placed finish in the Premier League. Gerard Houllier opted against giving Anelka a permanent deal at Liverpool and he ended up at Manchester City.

He came back to haunt the Reds after scoring a brace in a 2-1 win over them in May 2003. Throughout his career, Anelka scored 223 goals for club and country, winning two Champions League titles and the European Championship with France.

‌



PSG title winner

View 4 Images Mamadou Sakho was a title winner before he arrived at Anfield (Image: VI Images via Getty Images)

Mamadou Sakho had already made 201 appearances for PSG before his £18million move to Liverpool in 2013. The defender had won the Ligue 1 title just weeks before he joined the Reds, bringing a wealth of experience to Brendan Rodgers' side.

Sakho would go on to make 80 appearances for Liverpool, scoring three goals and continuing his time at Anfield after Rodgers was sacked in 2016. Jurgen Klopp kept the centre-half around for a half a season before Crystal Palace signed him on loan.

Article continues below

After an impressive temporary spell, Sakho would sign a permanent move to Palace in 2017 for a fee of £26m. He would go on to have stints at Montpellier and Torpedo Kutaisi before retiring in January this year at 35.

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott opens up on Aston Villa loan nightmare and second chance at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott opens up on Aston Villa loan nightmare and second chance at Liverpool

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott has spoken out about his future under Andoni Iraola after spending a season on the sidelines at Aston Villa under Unai Emery

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott has already featured in two friendlies for Andoni Iraola this summer (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Harvey Elliott believes he has been gifted a second chance at Liverpool after the arrival of Andoni Iraola, following a disastrous loan to Aston Villa last season. The former Fulham youngster is back with the Reds for pre-season and has already featured for his new boss as he looks to take the opportunity to impress.

‌



The midfielder made just one Premier League start during his time at Villa Park and nine appearances in all due to a clause in his loan which would have triggered a £35m transfer after his tenth appearance. Elliott was left out of squads throughout the season as he struggled to play under Unai Emery.

‌



It was not the season Elliott wanted, having only started twice in the Premier League during Arne Slot's title-winning season at Anfield. It cost him any chance of making it into Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad and leaves him desperate to play football.

‌



Elliott holds no ill will toward Villa but is now firmly focused on establishing himself at Liverpool. He believes that with a new coaching staff to impress, he has the perfect opportunity to rekindle his career.

“Unfortunately, it didn't work out, but the way I see it is that's last season now, I'm here. It's kind of a second chance, if you want to call it," Elliott explained.

Liverpool's significant Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG close in on replacement READ MORE :

Rio Ngumoha provides Bradley Barcola transfer hint as Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York READ MORE :

“Especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in. It's another chance to impress and hopefully get in their (good) books.

‌



"But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best, had a lot of love for them, and they treated me very, very well. Unfortunately, the situation happened, but It's another learning curve.

“It's a situation that I can take on in my career, and just keep looking forward. I'm here now, and I'm trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad."

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott barely featured for Aston Villa last season but did win the Europa League (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

While Elliott is looking to move on from last season, he conceded it was a difficult situation to bear. The 23-year-old was pleased to be part of an historic Europa League win with Villa but endured a draining situation on the sidelines.

“Mentally, it was a very tough one," he added. "As I said, it was a learning curve. It was an opportunity for me to experience something new, as much as I didn't want to do it, and I don't wish it upon any other player, because it's not nice at all, but I have no hard feelings.

‌



“I wish them all the very best. Well, I did greatly have a lot of love for them. They treated me as one of their own, as it were, and for that. I respect them highly.

“But it was tough, mentally and physically, but I'm on the other side of it now. I was able to get through it, and achieve something at the end of the season as well (with Villa winning the Europa League).

“That was another historical moment for the club, and to be part of that was another great situation. But my focus is on this season, at Liverpool, and I just need to see what happens.”

Sports.title: Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta

Arsenal have been chasing a deal for Bruno Guimaraes for weeks and a deal to bring the midfielder to north London is now closer - even though Newcastle are reluctant sellers

View 2 Images Arsenal are moving closer to a deal for Bruno Guimaraes (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Arsenal are now said to be 'increasingly confident' when it comes to their chances of clinching a deal for the wantaway Newcastle captain, Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



The Gunners have been pursuing Guimaraes all summer, making the Brazil international a priority transfer target. He is wanted to beef up Arsenal's midfield as Mikel Arteta and Co attempt to enhance a squad which not only won the Premier League last season for the first time in more than 20 years but also reached the Champions League final.

‌



It has been an open secret that Guimaraes is keen on the opportunity to compete for major trophies with Arsenal, even though Newcastle have no desire to sell their captain.

‌



However, it now seems as though the 28-year-old will get his wish with BBC Sport reporting that multiple sources now expect Guimaraes to join Arsenal.

Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure READ MORE :

Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure READ MORE :

It's added that although Newcastle are still reluctant to admit defeat in their attempts to keep Guimaraes at St James' Park, Arsenal are hopeful of closing a deal worth around the £80million mark in the coming days.

The news will come as a major boost for Arteta, who has already seen the club miss out on their top target for the left-wing berth, Morgan Rogers.

‌



Guimaraes would become the latest high-profile player to depart the Magpies if Arsenal can strike an agreement with Newcastle, with personal terms already done and dusted.

View 2 Images It emerged on Thursday that Eddie Howe has left Newcastle

Alexander Isak effectively went on strike last summer to clinch a £120m move to Liverpool, while Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have already been sold earlier in the current transfer window for significant fees to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively.

‌



Not only are Newcastle now likely to lose another talismanic player, but their head coach, Eddie Howe, is also moving on.

It emerged on Thursday morning that Howe had informed Newcastle's top brass that he wished to stand down from his role in order to take a break.

The former Bournemouth chief is poised to be replaced by Matthias Jaissle, the German coach currently in charge of Saudi Pro League outfit, Al-Ahli.

Sports.title: Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double
Sports.content:
Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double

Dan King, 21, who has been tipped to go all the way to the top, became the first rider for 42 years to win both the Galway Plate and Galway Hurdle

View 2 Images Dan King with his two Galway trophies (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

Rising star jump jockey Dan King made history on Thursday when he completed a huge Galway Festival double.

‌



The 21-year-old, who has been tipped to go all the way to the top in his profession, underlined his potential by pulling off a feat that had not been done for 42 years.

‌



On Wednesday, King netted the biggest prize of his burgeoning career as King Alexander defied odds of 20-1 to give Willie Mullins a third victory in the Galway Plate. The combination moved effortlessly into the lead from long-time leader Nouvotic at the second-last fence and ground it out from fast finisher Conyers Hill to win by half a length.

‌



Less than 24 hours after that success he rode Putapoundinthejar to capture the Guinness Galway Hurdle

Saving ground the whole way on the 10-1 winner, who was giving trainer Tony Martin his fifth victory in the race, King and Putapoundinthejar led at the final flight to beat Thisistheway by three and a quarter lengths.

‌



“It was plain sailing the whole way round,” he said after emulating the late Joe Byrne who was successful aboard Master Player and Tara Lee in 1984.

View 2 Images Daniel King (centre) riding Putapoundinthejar celebrates as he wins the Guinness Galway Hurdle (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

“He jumped savage the whole way round - he didn’t miss a beat. I took a chance going round the inside but when I wanted the gaps to open up they did.

Article continues below

“I’d never ridden a winner at the Galway Festival before but I was hopeful - I was coming here this week with a few nice rides. “When you get two of the biggest pots of the week, it’s class. “Dream stuff.”

Martin added of Putapoundinthejar: “He’s a big, old-fashioned horse. He was only coming to himself since Christmas and hopefully he’ll go on improving.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino MUST GO - FIFA chief has no way back after brutal response to World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Over the course of the World Cup, Gianni Infantino attended 45 matches and was captured by television cameras at every one of them.

Rarely was there a moment when he was not wearing a smug look. Record-breaking commercial income was on its way, stadiums were full and he had a $20billion trick up his sleeve - he was going to flog off the rights to the greatest sporting show on earth to private investors, dressing it up as a way of making extra cash for FIFA’s 211 member nations.

Well, 55 of those member nations have told him what he can do with his scheme. Ditch it. Or face not having a World Cup at all. Or a Women’s World Cup. Or a Club World Cup. Or any FIFA-organised World Cup.

Because without the European nations, there is no World Cup, of any kind. You can bet Gianni is not looking so smug today.

‌



UEFA could not have been more unequivocal. A truly unprecedented statement read: “No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.”

UEFA statement in FULL as they boycott World Cup until FIFA abandon controversial proposal READ MORE :

England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan READ MORE :

But the UEFA statement goes way, way beyond announcing a boycott of FIFA competitions, in itself a genuinely seismic decision in the history of football governance.

It lacerates Infantino’s integrity and morality. It lays his fitness for purpose to waste.

When talking of it being ‘irresponsible and indefensible’ that the FIFA proposal was ‘conceived in secret’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

‌



When talking of a ‘profound failure of leadership’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

When talking of ‘an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

When talking of ‘governance by intimidation’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

This is UEFA, the association whose teams dominate the World Cup. The powerhouse association of world football. The association who provided six of the eight quarter-finalists at World Cup 2026.

‌



And in their landmark emergency meeting, they not only made sure Infantino’s outlandish scheme is dead in the water, they clinically and viciously dismantled the character of the man in charge of world football, the man who Donald Trump believes would make a good Secretary General of NATO.

Well, perhaps Trump can get his mate the NATO gig because his position as FIFA president is now untenable. Infantino’s thick skin is the stuff of legend but it is impossible to see how he can stay in his post after this evisceration.

The statement from UEFA is pretty grand in its own morality.

‌



It concludes: “Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

It needs to be said that UEFA have not been slow to commercialise European football but that is another story.

They have been gunning for Infantino for some time, certainly since he launched the expanded Club World Cup.

And with this disgraceful, ill-judged, avaricious, mood-ignorant plot of his, Infantino has left himself open to be taken down.

‌



UEFA have taken their chance with cold brutality. Infantino has to go.

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Friday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Friday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

View 8 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Coral Goodwood Handicap: DEFIANTLY narrowly missed out on a marquee success at Royal Ascot - but compensation is at hand. The son of Kameko is something of a slow burn - he didn’t race at two and managed one victory, in a Killarney maiden, from four starts as a three-year-old in 2025.

‌



There was very little to write home about when Defiantly finished last of 18 at Cork in April on his handicap debut, an effort which persuaded Joseph O’Brien to reach for the headgear.

‌



There was more encouragement in his visored fourth to stablemate Kizlyar in a conditions race over a mile and three-quarters back at Killarney the following month, but punters still let the four-year-old go off at 25-1 for the return to handicaps in the Ascot Stakes over an additional six furlongs.

‌



With his headgear cranked up to blinkers, Defiantly thrived for the step up to the marathon distance, hitting the front inside the final half mile and engaging in a stirring battle with old rival Kizlyar, just coming off the worse by a head.

Dylan Browne McMonagle’s mount is 4lb higher in the weights but is unexposed over a distance of ground and gets the vote to go one better. Alphonse Le Grande , Believitanducan and Maxi King are all strong candidates for the podium.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 DEFIANTLY, 2 ALPHONSE LE GRANDE, 3 MAXI KIN

‌



View 8 Images Talk Of New York: Newsboy's pick (Image: PA)

2.25 HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes: TALK OF NEW YORK enjoys a significant drop in class and should get back to winning ways. The son of Wootton Bassett - dam Usherette was a two-time winner at Group 2 level in the care of André Fabre - looked potentially out of the ordinary when scoring by five and a half lengths at Kempton Park last October on his racecourse debut.

The Charlie Appleby trainee’s tendency to race with the choke out proved his undoing when third in Listed grade at Meydan in February, so it was little surprise to see Talk Of New York wearing a hood when he reappeared at Newmarket’s Craven meeting in April.

‌



William Buick’s mount justified odds of 8-11 for a seven-furlong conditions stakes with ease and was even more impressive when landing the Listed Heron Stakes over a mile at Sandown Park next time.

That success, a five-and-a-half-length humbling of Time To Turn, pre-empted a step up to the top tier for the St James’s Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot.

Talk Of New York was anything but discredited in the meeting’s Tuesday feature, finishing a length and three-quarters back in third as Bow Echo denied Gstaad by a short head.

‌



It goes without saying that this rates a much less exacting task and there will be long faces at Moulton Paddocks if Talk Of New York doesn’t take advantage. Shayem is improving and is the choice to chase the favourite home, ahead of Saber Strike and Yazin .

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 TALK OF NEW YORK, 2 SHAYEM, 3 SABER STRIKE

View 8 Images David Menuisier: trainer of Tribal Chief (Image: PA)

‌



3.00 Coral Golden Mile: TRIBAL CHIEF keeps threatening to land a big one - and today could be the day.

There’s no getting away from the fact the David Menuisier-saddled son of Sioux Nation comes with risks attached - invariably left at the back of the field by a sluggish start, he needs a decent gallop to aim at and for the gaps to appear.

But his record over the past 12 months makes Tribal Chief a danger to all when he finally gets the breaks.

‌



A staying-on sixth in this race last year, my selection netted a valuable course-and-distance handicap 23 days later, beating Treble Tee by half a length.

Out of luck in the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket and the Balmoral Handicap on Champions Day at Ascot on his final two outings of 2025, Tribal Chief stormed home to take third behind Urban Lion in the Lincoln at Doncaster in March on his return.

Seven furlongs for Ascot’s Victoria Cup next time was on the short side but the five-year-old was again strong at the finish for a third to The Wizard Of Eye, before a sixth to Indalo on Sandown Park’s Coral-Eclipse undercard, when the leaders didn’t go quick enough.

‌



But there should be a fair pace up front here and there’s no better man to execute a hold-up gameplan than Jamie Spencer. The Golden Mile is its usual headscratcher, with Blue Brother, Bunyola Bay, Cerulean Bay and Mister Winston just four horses capable of getting involved.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3, 1 TRIBAL CHIEF, 2 BLUE BROTHER, 3 CERULEAN BAY

View 8 Images Newsboy tips Rumstar to be out in front at Goodwood (Image: PA)

‌



3.35 King George Qatar Stakes - RUMSTAR is a four-time Group 3 winner who gives the strong impression he can make his presence felt at a higher level.

Jonathan Portman’s stable stalwart, a nursery winner here in July 2022, opened his account at Pattern level in the Cornwallis Stakes at Newmarket the following October, doubling up in the

Palace House Stakes on the 2,000 Guineas undercard in May 2025. And the son of Havana Grey has completed the quartet in the past two runnings of the Coral Charge at Sandown Park on the first Saturday of July, most recently when getting the better of Luna A Inbhir by one length.

‌



But Group 3 sprints shouldn’t be the ceiling of Rumstar’s ambitions, as demonstrated by his four luckless forays into Group 1 company.

The five-year-old was drawn away from the action when debuting in the top tier with a 14th-of-20 finish in the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last year, before being tightened for room when fifth to Asfoora in York’s Nunthorpe Stakes a couple of months later.

The draw gods again refused to play ball in the Prix de l’Abbaye at Longchamp in October and in this year’s King Charles III Stakes. Rumstar beat just one home on both occasions.

‌



But Rob Hornby’s partner went under by just half a length to today’s favourite Night Raider in Newmarket’s Palace House Stakes on his previous start and, with a decent pace in prospect, this race should be run to suit. Night Raider is greatly respected, along with Jakajaro and defending champion Jm Jungle.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 RUMSTAR, 2 NIGHT RAIDER, 3 JAKAJARO

View 8 Images Andrew Balding: trainer of Jonquil (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

‌



4.10 Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes: JONQUIL, proven at Group 2 level at Goodwood, gets the vote to bounce back to form after sub-optimal showings on his last two starts.

The son of Lope De Vega will return empty-handed to Andrew Balding’s Kingsclere stable if he can’t improve on a ninth-of-10 finish behind Notable Speech in the Group 1 Lockinge Stakes at Newbury in May or when beating one of seven opponents to the post in the Group 2 Summer Mile won by Zeus Olympios at Ascot 20 days ago.

But Jonquil was on-song prior to those disappointments, getting the better of the smart Holloway Boy by a length and a quarter for the Listed Paradise Stakes over a mile at Ascot at the beginning of May.

‌



And, while he didn’t shine in a messy running of the Group 2 Lennox Stakes won by Witness Stand when making his Goodwood debut at this fixture 12 months ago, Colin Keane’s mount showed the South Downs hold no terrors for him when accounting for Saqqara Sands by a neck in the Group 2 Celebration Mile next time.

An additional furlong here won’t be an issue for a colt who is very much a player if bringing his best form to the table. Galen, Boiling Point and Crown Of Oaks can fight it out for silver and bronze.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 JONQUIL, 2 GALEN, 3 CROWN OF OAKS

‌



View 8 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

4.45 Hawes And Curtis Nursery Handicap: REVELS looks fairly treated for his first appearance in the handicap sphere.

The son of Lope De Vega - dam Snooze N You Lose was a Listed winner for my selection’s trainer Karl Burke - fetched 350,000 guineas a yearling and had clearly been showing up prior to his debut at Redcar in May.

‌



Revels went off at 8-11 in a field of seven and his supporters were spared any anxious moments as he strolled clear under Sam James to win by three lengths.

Given his debut promise, the chestnut put up a so-so effort when 9th of 14 behind Nola Soul in the Listed Chesham Stakes at Royal Ascot last time - but there were excuses.

Drawn in stall two, Revels raced on the far side of the pack, occupying a track position that didn’t show him to best advantage.

‌



The evidence of his first start is Revels has the speed to cope with the step back from seven furlongs to six and he has plenty of potential to go past an opening British Horseracing Authority rating of 85.

In a field of two-year-olds whose best days lie ahead, Dubai Champion, Clash Of Hearts and Paper View are just three runners who merit a second glance.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 REVELS, 2 DUBAI CHAMPION, 3 PAPER VIEW

‌



View 8 Images Charlie Appleby: trainer of Into The Light (Image: Getty Images)

5.20 World Pool Bet with the Tote Handicap: INTO THE LIGHT didn’t shine when fancied to go well at Royal Ascot, but it’s early days to be writing him off.

Unraced at two, Dubawi’s son began to make up for lost time when lifting a 10-furlong maiden at Lingfield Park on St Valentine’s Day by a length from Al Azd.

‌



Into The Light finished a three-length second to Ravenspire when upped to a mile and a half at Southwell the following month and again claimed the silver medal when beaten a short-head by the progressive Lost Boys over two furlongs shorter at Sandown Park next time when making his handicap debut.

Charlie Appleby then sent my selection for the King George V Handicap at the royal meeting and punters liked Into The Light’s chances - he went off at 4-1 in a field of 19.

Things didn’t work out - William Buick’s mount came back in 11th of 19 behind Enceladus - but Into The Light, equipped with cheekpieces, retains potential and can go well. Kenergy is far from exposed and makes appeal, in company with Pierian and Mythical Valentine.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 INTO THE LIGHT, 2 KENERGY, 3 PIERIAN

View 8 Images James Fanshawe trains Newsboy's tip

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
