World.title: Berlin Pride attack: Are German juvenile courts too lenient?
World.content:
The Islamist terror attack on Berlin Pride has put the work of juvenile courts into the spotlight. Many argue the 21-year-old perpetrator should have been in prison at the time of the attack.

Could the terrorist attack on Berlin's Pride celebrations, allegedly by a 21-year-old Islamist, have been prevented? This question has been the subject of debate driven largely by the fact that the young German man — born in Germany in 2005 to parents of Lebanese origin — had been convicted and released just weeks before the attack.

Abdul Ballout, who drove his car into a crowd in Berlin's Tiergarten park — killing one woman and injuring 31 people, some seriously — had set out last year intending to join the so-called "Islamic State" (IS) terrorist group in Syria. However, he was arrested en route in Lebanon, detained there and subsequently deported to Germany.

Back in Germany, he stood trial on charges of preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state. He was found guilty and sentenced in mid-May to 22 months in prison, but this sentence was initially suspended. He was released — and attacked Berlin Pride just weeks later. The day after the incident, he was shot dead by police while they were attempting to arrest him.

Police 'should have kept an eye on' Berlin Pride attacker To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Juvenile sentencing can be applied to up to 20-year-olds because the brain is still developing at that age

Since then, juvenile criminal law in Germany has been the focus of criticism. Terrorism expert Peter Neumann from King's College London told the news portal T-Online: "This is a real problem. The sentences are too lenient. In my view, juvenile criminal law is sometimes interpreted too broadly. The protection of the public is not given sufficient consideration."

Juvenile criminal law serves special purposes, says Frieder Dünkel, a criminologist and criminal law expert from Greifswald. "It's primarily about education, about the reintegration of the young person," he told DW.

Judges have considerable leeway and can hand out admonitions or prison sentences.

In Germany, a perpetrator is criminally responsible from age 14 and juvenile criminal law applies. From the age of 18, regular criminal law generally applies, with higher minimum sentences. But juvenile criminal law can also be applied to young adults aged 18 to 20 if they show "developmental delays."

"This is because overall, one can still recognize significant developmental potential in 18- to 20-year-olds," Dünkel said.

This is backed by neuroscientific findings, according to Dünkel, showing that the brain areas responsible for behavioral control do not fully develop until the middle of the third decade of life. This implies that a young offender can still change for the better.

In May, Abdul Ballout was sentenced by the Berlin court under juvenile criminal law, even though he was already 21 at the time of his sentencing. However, he was only 20 years old when he committed the crimes he was found guilty of.

Berlin attack: When deradicalization programs don't work To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

'Preliminary probation' for Ballout

Ballout was able to leave the courthouse because he had been granted six months of "preliminary probation," after which the court would have had to make a final decision on whether he needed to go to prison. He was initially placed under intermittent police surveillance until the police officers concluded that he was behaving unobtrusively.

He was ordered to participate in an exit program for extremists, where he attended two preliminary meetings to determine whether he was indeed willing to critically examine his behavior and distance himself from extremism.

Preliminary probation is a relatively new concept in Germany's criminal law and was introduced in 2012. Frieder Dünkel believes that the mechanism has been successful in many cases.

"Specifically, when a juvenile court judge is unsure whether a sentence can or should be suspended in favor of probation, the judge orders a period of up to six months during which the young person is guided toward a law-abiding lifestyle through strict directives and monitoring measures," Dünkel explained.

German interior minister wants to reform juvenile criminal law

In the aftermath of the Berlin Pride attack, there have been calls to stop applying the more lenient juvenile criminal law to Islamist or right-wing extremist perpetrators.

But criminologist Dünkel disagrees: "It is not the role of juvenile criminal law to provide preventive protection for society before a crime has even been committed. Juvenile criminal law responds to crimes once they have been committed," he says.

Juvenile criminal law does allow for severe penalties; for instance, a murder conviction can result in a 15-year prison sentence for offenders aged 18 to 20.

Dünkel adds that recidivism rates among perpetrators sentenced under juvenile criminal law are no higher than among those sentenced under adult criminal law.

"Harsher penalties do not lead to greater security," he said.

Nevertheless, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) has announced his intention to examine ways to reform juvenile criminal law.

Konstantin von Notz, the opposition Green Party's expert on internal affairs disagrees with that approach.

"We... note that virtually all experts consulted on this matter so far point out that long prison sentences — especially for young adults — can have a counterproductive effect and may even accelerate existing radicalization," von Notz said.

What does the Berlin Pride attack mean for city's identity? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Information sharing glitch

Ballout had been classified as a dangerous individual by Germany's Joint Counter-Terrorism Center (GTAZ). The GTAZ is a coordination and communication platform established in 2004, after the 9/11 terror attacks in the United States, to combat Islamist terrorism through inter-agency information sharing.

However, the assessment of Ballout did not reach the Berlin court that handed down the lenient sentence earlier this year. If the information had been shared, Ballout may have remained incarcerated.

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
World.content:
US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.

"I cannot live without looking over my shoulder," a sexual abuse survivor told US lawmakers in May, describing how her personal information was publicly exposed in January, when the Department of Justice (DOJ) released hundreds of thousands of documents related to the financier Jeffrey Epstein. "I can only imagine the long-term impact this mistake will have on my life."

Three days after the DOJ released the largest of 12 datasets on Epstein on January 30, a department lawyer told a federal court that "human or technical error" had been among the factors that led to the publishing of personally identifying information of people who had been sexually abused by Epstein and his associates. As a result, the DOJ said it would remove, review and redact flagged documents before republishing them.

DW's investigative unit, along with its Innovation and Data teams, spent months reviewing thousands of documents released by the DOJ. In the six months since the release, DW identified dozens of files that still contained information — including names, faces and email addresses — that could be used to identify survivors, witnesses and informants, among other people.

DOJ Epstein Library

By mid-February, DW had scraped more than 800,000 files from the DOJ's Epstein Library — a challenging task with the archive constantly changing: New files were being added, others were taken down and modified files were popping up after days of absence.

But it wasn't until DW obtained an earlier set of files archived by a publicly facing data preservation project on GitHub that we realized more than 500,000 files were removed between the initial days of the release and our scrape.

To verify the contents of the original release, DW generated a unique digital fingerprint, known as a hash, for every document. Hashes confirm that a document matches the original and hasn't been altered. By comparing these fingerprints with documents scraped from the DOJ website about two weeks later, DW could determine which files matched, as well as identify documents that had been removed from the DOJ website.

DW also found that some files had changed because the digital fingerprint was no longer the same: They had the same file name but were larger or smaller than the original. When DW reviewed this subset, we found that they represented files that had been further redacted — or information was added.

In one instance, a survivor described how Epstein had abused her for years as a minor in her testimony to lawyers. Her name was redacted throughout the transcript until the last page, when a lawyer thanked her for her testimony and said her name, and it remains unredacted as of publication.

Her exposed name was not an isolated case.

US lawmakers created strict rules on how the Epstein files should be published, such as ensuring that personally identifying information of victims be redacted to protect them from public exposure Image: picture-alliance/dpa/M. Reynolds

Deep audio analysis

To analyze audio files, including victim statements and tipoffs, DW's investigative unit collaborated with the Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Media Technology's Media Distribution and Security research group in Ilmenau, Germany. The MDS specializes in audio authenticity, manipulation and speech synthesis detection.

After removing duplicated files from the publicly facing data preservation project and DW's scrape, we were left with more than 150 audio files, which the MDS's forensic audio researchers analyzed using state-of-the-art tools developed at the institute. They detected digital traces left by audio production and editing processes that are, at times, inaudible to the human ear.

That included identifying parts of a recording that had been modified or reused, determining whether a recording was an altered version of another file, and assessing whether audio files may have been recorded using the same microphone or recording setup.

Forensic audio researcher Milica Gerhardt observed something unique: that redaction styles varied across the files, along with inconsistencies in how redactions were executed.

"If one observes the content of these audio files, one can see that a lot of personal information has not been redacted," Gerhardt said.

Using the Audio Provenance Suite App, Gerhardt identified two files in the same dataset with identical content, but one was redacted and the other unredacted Image: Stefan Czimmek/DW

In one case, a person called an official tipoff hotline to report information for use in an investigation into Epstein's abuse. In the redacted version, you can hear the person's name, but their phone number was bleeped out.

The same dataset, however, also contained a different version of the audio file, in which the person's full name could be heard as well as their direct contact. Alleged witnesses or informants were apparently not included in the protections allotted to victims.

"They could and should have done a better job on the redactions," said Patrick Aichroth, who heads the MDS group at the Fraunhofer Institute, which has consulted on audio-related evidence for judicial authorities in Germany.

"There is a reason why such material is treated so carefully in court cases," Aichroth said. "Once sensitive or identifying information is disclosed, the damage cannot be undone."

Redactions across audio files were inconsistent and revealed sensitive information, according to audio forensics researchers. Image: Stefan Czimmek/DW

DOJ's redaction failures

DW's investigative unit confronted the DOJ with its findings, including examples in which survivors' personally identifiable information remained in the official Epstein Library.

The DOJ did not respond.

In April, the DOJ's Office of the Inspector General, an independent watchdog tasked with investigating misconduct within the department, announced that it was "initiating an audit of DOJ's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act."

"Our preliminary objective is to evaluate the DOJ's processes for identifying, redacting and releasing records in its possession as required by the Act," the office said in a statement.

In July, several lawmakers introduced the Epstein Files Transparency Act II, which would allow sexual abuse survivors and the governments of US states to take the DOJ to court for failing to comply with the rules laid out in the initial Transparency Act, which had guaranteed that the personally identifiable information of survivors would be protected.

Survivors whose information was published unredacted have since shared accounts of harassment, humiliation and physical threats. With the publicly disclosed information still available on public platforms and, in some cases, still on the DOJ website, the impact continues to upend survivors' lives.

"While the rich and powerful remain protected by redactions, my name was exposed to the world," said the sexual abuse survivor who gave her testimony to Congress in May.

"The evidence is right here," she said, "yet those in power [would] rather us die socially, emotionally and physically than admit their own complicity."

Edited by: Mathias Bölinger, Milan Gagnon

Technical and data analysis by: Andreas Giefer

Data journalists: Gianna Grün, Rodrigo Menegat Schuinski

Fact checking by: Birgitta Schülke

World.title: UEFA votes to boycott World Cup over FIFA investor plan
World.content:
UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott ‌the ⁠World ⁠Cup and other competitions unless FIFA abandons its private investor plans. "The World Cup is not for sale," they said, as FIFA seeks to sell a stake in it.

European football's governing body, UEFA, called a Thursday afternoon meeting of its 55 members to discuss a response to FIFA's plans to create a new commercial subsidiary valued at $20 billion (roughly €17.5 billion) and sell a non-controlling minority stake in it to investors.

In the meeting, the members voted unanimously to boycott FIFA competitions in protest of the plan.

"No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership," UEFA said in a statement.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product... No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale," the statement added.

Shortly after, North America’s soccer body CONCACAF unanimously rejected the FIFA plan, though it stopped short of a boycott.

UEFA swiftly rejected FIFA's proposal

UEFA had come out publicly in opposition to the plan within an hour of it first being reported by the Financial Times and Times on Tuesday.

Shortly after the newspaper reports, FIFA, the sport's global governing body, issued a statement confirming the plan.

In a later statement, it gave FIFA's 211 member associations until September 19 to express their written support for the scheme. The proposal requires a simple majority and approval from the FIFA Council to pass.

Even before Thursday's meeting, UEFA had doubled down on its criticism after learning of the deadline, saying: "Today we have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything ​you need to know about this plan.

Aleksander Ceferin's UEFA has been at loggerheads with FIFA for some time Image: Mike Egerton/PA/picture alliance

It added that talks with many stakeholders showed that "there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme. FIFA cannot to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends."

DFB: FIFA plan 'problematic and unacceptable'

Germany's mass-circulation Bild paper reported that key UEFA officials including German FA (DFB) President Bernd Neuendorf had already discussed the FIFA plans via a video call on Wednesday.

"We must not lose the fans' support, but we are well on the way to squandering that," he told public broadcaster ZDF. "I consider this to be extremely problematic and unacceptable.

"If UEFA rejects this request (for approval of the plan), then it is dead, because I believe that you won't be able to find any investor who would be willing to go ahead with this project if UEFA is out," he added.

Bernd Neuendorf can't see the FIFA plan going forward without UEFA on board Image: Ulrich Wagner/picture alliance

Other critics have expressed fears that the deal could lead to more tournaments, teams and matches to increase revenue and boost the value of investors' stakes.

UEFA hasn't been the only confederation to criticize the report. CONCACAF, responsible for North and Central America, as well as the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) have also expressed concerns that the proposal was made public without their consultation while the African confederation (CAF) have said they will discuss the plans next week.

Members of the FIFA Council, including Neuendorf, have said they were not consulted on the latest proposal.

FIFA: Subsidiary could raise billions 'this year'

FIFA has said the new subsidiary, to be known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) would be valued at $20 billion and that it would aim to raise up to $4.2 billion "this year" by "carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests" in the company. FFE would be responsible for FIFA's commercial rights like broadcast, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing contracts. By far the most valuable of these are those linked to the World Cup,

Under the ​plan, FIFA said it could make $10 billion available for development beginning in 2027. Each federation would be eligible for up to $20 ​million in one-time Fast Forward funding, in addition to $20 million through the regular FIFA Forward program during the 2027-30 ⁠cycle. Without ​approval, FIFA projects a development package of about $2.7 billion.

FIFA unveils controversial World Cup investor plan To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Infantino: 'A golden opportunity'

In face of the opposition, FIFA President Gianni Infantino released a video on Wednesday evening, describing the project a "golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally."

He added that the proposal was "part of a democratic process" and in comments directed to football fans, he stressed that "the sport they watch and love will not change."

Edited by: Matt Pearson

World.title: EU aims to build AI gigafactories of its own
World.content:
The EU has unveiled a plan to raise state and private funds to hyperscale AI capabilities and gain independence from non-European governments. The plan calls for the construction of seven new sites across the bloc.

The European Commission on Thursday announced a call for tenders designed to generate over €30 billion ($34 billion) in state and private funding for the construction of seven so-called AI gigafactories to boost the European Union's computing independence.

Of the funds, €10 billion will come from the EU and member states while private investors put up the remaining €20 billion.

The funds are to be collected and distributed by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) , which was launched in 2020 to develop "a world class supercomputing ecosystem by pooling the resources of the European Union, European countries and private partners."

Consortia and special ⁠purpose ​vehicles (SPVs) made up of technology and ​cloud service providers, public entities and investors are all eligible to apply for funding.

Chipmakers AMD, ​Nvidia and Qualcomm have all signed letters of intent to provide chips to groups involved in the projects, according to the Commission.

The Commission said the scheme will "expand Europe's AI computing capacity and give start-ups, scale-ups, small and medium-sized enterprises, industry, academia and public authorities access to infrastructure."

Speaking of the construction of the facilities — which will produce advanced AI processors, software and cloud technology stacks, high-speed connectivity and energy-efficient data centers — Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission's executive vice-president for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, called the moment "a milestone."

"Access to the raw scale of computing power within AI gigafactories is a strategic necessity for Europe as AI development accelerates," she said in a statement.

Can Germany and Europe hold their own in AI race? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

EU beholden to US and China when it comes to tech

Currently, the EU operates 19 data centers located between Spain and Finland.

The bloc remains heavily reliant upon foreign actors for its tech, however, something that makes it and its member states extremely vulnerable to the whims of outside forces.

US President Donald Trump, for instance, has made clear his intention to leverage American economic heft to influence how the bloc and its members regulate US tech.

For its part, China has limited the supply of minerals critical to the sector.

The EU now hopes to triple data center capacity within five to seven years in order to gain independence but sees challenges when competing with the US and China, where, among other things, energy is far cheaper.

A recent report issued by the European Commission and presented to the EU Parliament was bleak in its outlook should the situation remain as it is, warning, "European businesses and public authorities will continue to rely on US AI providers to the detriment of European service providers struggling to work at the frontier."

"Dependence on hyperscale cloud and AI computing service providers, particularly for highly critical use cases," the report said, "will continue to expose data to third-country access and carry risks to service continuity, endangering operational autonomy."

EU selling tech, are citizens willing to buy?

EU leaders have sounded the alarm over the bloc's lagging efforts on the AI front, yet some citizens are leery of the tech for a host of social, economic and environmental reasons.

The Commission has sought to allay fears with pledges that the new technology will be developed and operated according to "EU standards on data protection, safety, security and ethics," in reference to the bloc's Digital Services Act and Digital Market Act.

Beyond fears of massive job losses caused by AI, the construction of massive tech facilities has faced global backlash over environmental concerns due to their voracious appetite for water and electricity as well as the inordinate amount of noise pollution they produce.

The European Commission says it will accept bids for its new projects until November 12, and begin distributing funds in early 2027 so that construction can begin within the year.

World.title: Human trafficking in Mexico: the dark side of tourism
World.content:
By May, a record-breaking 20 million tourists had visited Mexico so far in 2026. But with increased tourism comes a heightened risk of human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Women and children are most vulnerable.

Warning: This article discusses sexual violence, which some readers might find distressing.

Mixi Cruz was just 13 years old when her mother died. At first, she lived on the streets, then she turned to her elder stepsister for help. Once there, she was forced to manage household chores and pressured into sexual exploitation.

"The hardest part was accepting that none of that happened simply because I was naive or stupid," the young woman, now 33, tells DW. "It happened to me because there are bad people who sell other people. And there are bad people who buy other people."

In Mexico human trafficking has become one of the most lucrative economies in organized crime. According to the 2025 Global Organized Crime Index by the Swiss-based Global Initiative organization combating transnational organized crime, criminal synidicates are becoming more and more involved. These include the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion, CJNG) and the Sinaloa Cartel.

Within just one year, the number of incidents reported to authorities spiked by 45%.

India's lost children at risk in rail stations To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

On World Day Against Trafficking in Persons, July 30, the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is calling for tighter, cross-border cooperation between judiciaries and law enforcement. Experts say that so far, only a fraction of the actual cases are being reported, let alone solved.

Perpetrators exploit vulnerabilities

Mixi Cruz was exploited by her own family. She was made to look after five children, and iron laundry until late at night. She still has scars on her hands, from when she'd fall asleep and burn herself with the iron, she says.

Not longer after, she was pressured into sex work for money. She was 14.

Many survivors don't know at the time that they are experiencing sexual violence, she says.

"Many think they're in love, or their own family sells them," Cruz explains. "From the time they're little, they're made to believe violence is normal, and just part of what love is."

Online sexual abuse of children in Philippines To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In Mexico, the civil-society organization Consejo Ciudadano para la Seguridad y Justicia (Citizens' Council for Security and Justice) estimates that seven out of 10 human trafficking survivors are female. More than half of them are minors.

Hidden human trafficking figure much higher, experts say

"Human trafficking is a game of deceit, it involves a high level of emotional manipulation to isolate victims and prevent them from reaching out and building support networks," Gabriela Gonzalez Garcia explains. She is the director general of citizen services for the Citizens' Council.

Her organization runs Mexico's only specialized 24-hour hotline , as well as a live chat, for people affected by human trafficking. Since it was founded in 2007, the organization has counted some 26,000 cases. But the real number, Gonzalez says, is far higher, likely around 98%.

Ana Torres and three volunteers are in a red-light district near the edge of Mexico City. She's asked not to be mentioned by her real name. Now in her late 20s, she's been leading a street project for the past five years for El Pozo de Vida ("The Well of Life" in Spanish) that combats human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Each week, Torres and her colleagues visit a different part of Mexico's capital, speaking with the women there and offering help.

Gabriela Gonzalez Garcia heads the non-profit organization Consejo Ciudadano, which operates Mexico's only 24-hour hotline for human trafficking victims Image: Consejo Ciudadano/Oliver Villalobos Méndez

Before this year's soccer World Cup in Mexico, Canada and the United States, many sex workers had hoped for higher earnings, but Torres says the demand remained virtually unchanged. But what did increase noticeably was the number of foreign tourists, and with it, another source of danger for the women on the streets: the language barrier.

"Maybe they reach an agreement (with clients) on the street," Torres explained. "But what really happens when they get a room?"

Raising awareness for human trafficking

The UNODC and its Mexican partners the like Citizens' Council used campaigns like Mundial sin Trata ("A World Cup Without Human Trafficking" in Spanish) to make the tourism industry more aware of the increased risk of human trafficking during the World Cup. A popular driving service joined the campaign, and an online homestay operator teamed up with the UNODC to offer workshops for hosts.

But Cruz says she's skeptical that was enough to curb trafficking and exploitation.

"Men don't pay for sex because they traveled here just for that. They do it because an opportunity presents itself," Cruz said. "In any tourist district, people can tell you where to find prostitution, where you can find women, or children."

Mixi Cruz was forced into sexual exploitation by her own family. Today, she raises awareness for the issue to protect others Image: Bastian Kaiser

'They're locked away and guarded'

In the red-light district, it's starting to rain. Many sex workers have disappeared into nearby houses. A young woman is standing at the corner, wearing black high-heels, a short green dress, grey denim jacket, dark hair to her shoulders. Rain drops bounce off her umbrella. Ana Torres approaches her.

The young woman says she's worried about one of her colleagues, from Colombia, who's currently hiding somewhere in the city. She talks about a family of pimps that targets Colombians, luring them to Mexico with fake promises.

The pimp's wife, she says, has an iron grip on operations: "She makes them work 12 to 15 hours a day, they're not even allowed to eat alone," the woman told DW. "They're locked away and guarded in houses."

Ana Torres asks the woman to pass her organization's number on to her colleague who has fled. The young woman has tears streaming down her face as Ana Torres commends her for her courage to speak up for others.

On the way back, Ana says she's under the impression the pimps and their overseers were watching the women more closely that evening than they usually would. She says she's not quite sure why, but it worries her.

Trapped in the human trafficking network To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Mixi Cruz was 16 when she finally managed to run away. Today, she's part of a survivors' network that visits schools and universities to raise awareness for human trafficking. Her stepsister was eventually sentenced to four years in prison, her stepsister's husband got five years. In the end, they weren't convicted for human trafficking, but for other serious offenses. But even that is unusual.

This article was translated from German.

If you or someone you know have experienced any kind of gender-based violence, the website lila.help lists trustworthy helplines and NGOs that offer support in almost every country in the world.

World.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | Al menos 10 migrantes han muerto al intentar entrar a nado en Ceuta
World.content:
Sánchez viaja mañana a Ceuta con Marlaska | Bruselas ofrece a España el apoyo de Frontex | Albares convoca al embajador de Italia en España tras afirmar Meloni que estudia suspender el acuerdo Schengen

Las fuerzas de seguridad han recuperado los cadáveres de 10 personas que intentaban entrar a nado en Ceuta, según fuentes policiales. El Gobierno ha decidido movilizar a las unidades del Ejército de Tierra para apoyar a los efectivos de la Guardia Civil, que se encuentran desbordados ante la entrada de miles de jóvenes que cruzan a nado la frontera del Tarajal que separa la ciudad española de Marruecos. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, viajará mañana al enclave, acompañado del ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska. Esta nueva oleada se suma a una crisis que presiona a la ciudad autónoma desde hace al menos una semana y que recuerda a la vivida en 2021, cuando unos 5.000 marroquíes cruzaron la frontera en un solo día. Bruselas ha trasladado la disposición de la Unión Europea a reforzar su apoyo a España, también mediante Frontex. Mientras, el Gobierno italiano estudia suspender el acuerdo de Schengen de libre circulación con España a raíz de la crisis migratoria, según ha anunciado la primera ministra, Giorgia Meloni. En respuesta, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, ha convocado al embajador de Italia en España.

EL PAÍS ofrece de forma gratuita la última hora de la crisis migratoria. Si quieres apoyar nuestro periodismo, suscríbete.

World.title: Detenidos dos hombres de 51 y 42 años como presuntos responsables del incendio de Almorox
World.content:
La Guardia Civil de Toledo ha detenido este jueves a dos hombres, de 51 y 42 años, como presuntos responsables del incendio de Almorox (Toledo) que el pasado 22 de julio se originó en una zona forestal de esta localidad propagándose a la Comunidad de Madrid. Los indicios recogidos en la investigación desarrollada por el Seprona y el Cuerpo de Agentes Medioambientales de la delegación provincial de Desarrollo Sostenible apuntan a una negligencia al realizar actividades prohibidas en riesgo “extremo” de incendios.

Fuentes de la investigación consultadas por EL PAÍS señalan que los detenidos estaban realizando trabajos de soldadura en una parcela dentro de un terreno forestal en la localidad toledana. Los agentes localizaron el punto de inicio del incendio, donde hallaron “indicios concluyentes de la ejecución reciente de trabajos de soldadura sobre una estructura metálica ubicada en terreno forestal”, recoge una nota del instituto armado. Este tipo de actividades estaban prohibidas el día que se originó el incendio al encontrarse el Índice de Propagación Potencial (IPP) en nivel “extremo”.

Vista de una calle, a 25 de julio de 2026, en Almorox, hasta donde llegaba el humo del incendio originado en el municipio. Juanma Jiménez (Europa Press)

El fuego se detectó el pasado 22 de julio a las 16.52 en el paraje Pino de la Parra, en una finca propiedad de uno de los dos detenidos. El avance de las llamas obligó a evacuar dos urbanizaciones, El Pinar de Almorox y El Encinar del Alberche, en el municipio madrileño de Villa del Prado, que también tuvo que ser confinado. Las llamas destruyeron al menos 43 viviendas y otras 286 casas sufrieron daños de diversa consideración. Fue el germen de uno de los grandes incendios de la Sierra Oeste de Madrid, uno de los más grandes de los últimos años en España con unas 30.000 hectáreas afectadas.

Los detenidos han prestado declaración ante el juez titular de la plaza número 2 de la Sección Civil y de Instrucción del Tribunal de Instancia de Torrijos (Toledo), en funciones de guardia, por un presunto delito contra el medio ambiente, según fuentes del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Castilla-La Mancha. Ambos han quedado en libertad provisional con medidas cautelares: se les ha retirado el pasaporte, no podrán salir del territorio nacional y deberán comparecer ante el juzgado todos los lunes. La imputación es provisional y se tendrá que concretar a lo largo de la investigación judicial.

World.title: La extraña reinvención de Drea de Matteo, de Los Soprano: OnlyFans y el movimiento ultra son su segunda vida
World.content:
Ganó un Emmy y fue una de las actrices más queridas de la televisión. Dos décadas después, la neoyorquina vende contenido en la plataforma para adultos, presenta un ‘podcast’ con figuras de la derecha alternativa y asegura que Hollywood la castigó por su negativa a vacunarse

En septiembre de 2004, Drea de Matteo vivió el mejor momento de su vida profesional. En su primera y única nominación, la intérprete que había dado vida a Adriana La Cerva en Los Soprano se alzó con el Emmy a mejor actriz de reparto tras cinco temporadas en la celebrada serie. “Hay muchas personas responsables de esto, pero si intento dar las gracias a cualquiera de ellas ahora mismo, podría vomitar, atragantarme, llorar o morir. Ya me habéis visto hacer todo eso”, alegaba con sarcasmo sobre el escenario. El galardón parecía el detonante definitivo de una de las carreras más prometedoras del elenco de una ficción que ya enfilaba su recta final. Siendo una actriz desconocida en la industria, trascendió el papel de novia del joven mafioso Christopher Moltisanti gracias a la vulnerabilidad y humanidad de un personaje atrapado en una espiral de violencia, dependencia emocional y sueños frustrados.

Michael Imperioli y Drea De Matteo en una imagen promocional de HBO para Los Soprano. Anthony Neste (Getty Images)

Sus personajes eran Christopher Moltisanti y Adriana La Cerva. Getty Images (Getty Images)

También se convirtió en un sex symbol, habitual en las listas de las mujeres más deseadas del mundo, y en todo un icono de estilo Y2K con sus minifaldas, estampados de leopardo, pantalones de cuero y el volumen hipertrofiado de su melena rubia, una estética reivindicada años después con el auge de la tendencia mob wife. La trágica resolución de su destino sigue considerándose una de las grandes escenas de la historia de la televisión, pero su protagonista nunca logró replicar la dimensión mediática de su primer gran personaje. Ahora, 22 años después, sí lo está consiguiendo, pero lejos ya de los focos de la meca del cine.

Drea de Matteo ha vuelto a los titulares, pero no por sus logros artísticos. Una cuenta de OnlyFans, un discurso feroz contra Hollywood y una marca antisistema la han convertido en una de las grandes voces del ámbito ultra de Estados Unidos. “Soy una zorra controvertida”, se define a sí misma en su nueva faceta como creadora de contenido. Ultrafree (Ultralibre) es el nombre del podcast presentado por De Matteo y en el que cada semana aboga por cuestionar el llamado “Estado profundo” y participar en la guerra cultural dando voz a activistas antisistema, figuras canceladas y conspiranoicos varios. Del supuesto poder de las farmacéuticas y la vigilancia gubernamental a conversaciones sobre el Apocalipsis, los chemtrails, la censura de las grandes tecnológicas o las terapias alternativas contra el cáncer, el universo de Ultrafree se mueve entre el libertarismo radical y el cuestionamiento permanente de las instituciones. Para completar el negocio, una marca de ropa de nombre homónimo que viste su filosofía con sudaderas oversize, colores neutros y grandes logotipos con lemas como Anti Bullshit (“Antimierdas”), más cercanos al merchandising de una tribu digital que a una firma de moda convencional.

Drea de Matteo en un estreno en Manhatta en 2022. Paul Archuleta (Getty Images)

Según sostiene la artista natural de Queens (Nueva York), de 54 años, esta nueva aventura empresarial es la única manera que encontró para salir a flote tras haber sido defenestrada por Hollywood. En su versión, fue víctima de una industria que renegó de ella después de negarse a vacunarse contra la COVID-19. Casi de manera instantánea, asegura, sus amigos del cine se alejaron, su representante la abandonó y las ofertas de trabajo cayeron en picado. Con apenas diez dólares en el banco y a punto de perder su casa por el impago de la hipoteca, De Matteo siguió el consejo de sus hijos adolescentes y abrió una cuenta en la plataforma de contenido para adultos OnlyFans con una fotografía en bikini. Quince dólares por suscripción para acceder a lo que ella misma definió como “porno de abuela”. Según su propio relato, en apenas cinco minutos, había ingresado unos 75.000 dólares, suficientes para evitar el embargo de su vivienda. “OnlyFans me salvó la vida por completo. Cualquiera que quiera condenarme y menospreciarme, adelante. Solo espero que nunca se encuentren en la situación en la que yo me vi para sacar adelante a dos niños pequeños. Salvó el hogar en el que he vivido durante muchos años y que era muy importante para nosotros. Y, más allá de todo eso, me ha dado suficiente dinero para poner en marcha y financiar Ultrafree”, confesó al Daily Mail.

Recogiendo el Emmy. Michael Caulfield Archive (WireImage)

Su evolución ideológica es llamativa. Aunque durante su carrera como actriz apenas habló de política e incluso confesó haber votado al candidato demócrata Joe Biden en 2020, de un tiempo a esta parte De Matteo se ha convertido en una de las mayores defensoras del presidente Donald Trump, a quien ha llegado a describir como “the big daddy” (“el gran papá”). También ha evidenciado su postura antiaborto y ha asegurado que Hollywood es una industria “salvaje” con quienes no siguen las reglas marcadas. Ni siquiera algunos de los sectores más conservadores de la opinión pública, que suelen concordar con muchos de sus preceptos, la respaldaron cuando reveló que era su hijo de 12 años –tiene dos, fruto de su relación con el productor musical Shooter Jennings– quien editaba parte de las fotografías sugerentes que después publicaba en OnlyFans. “Fueron los niños los que me dijeron: “Haz esto. Enseña los pies. ¡Hazte selfies! J.Lo y las Kardashian siempre están en bikini en internet, ¿por qué tú no?”, añade. El secreto de su éxito como modelo erótica está, según corrobora, en los carbohidratos: “Antes de cada foto como mucho, no salgo bien en ellas si estoy flaca. Soy una dama italiana atiborrándome a pasta y filetes. Quieres que tus pechos y tu culo se vean grandes. De lo contrario, las fotos son un festival de bostezos”, sostiene la actriz, que comparte su vida actualmente con el guitarrista Robbie Staebler.

Aunque De Matteo insiste en que su rechazo a los mandatos sanitarios la acabó metiendo en una lista negra en Hollywood, lo cierto es que su carrera llevaba años pidiendo reinvención. Como les ocurre a muchos actores que crean un personaje inolvidable, nunca logró escapar del todo de la sombra de Adriana La Cerva. Con el empuje mediático de Los Soprano consiguió un papel protagonista en Joey, el spin-off de Friends, dando vida a la hermana del personaje de Matt LeBlanc, pero la serie fue cancelada tras apenas dos temporadas. Después llegarían trabajos en ficciones como Hijos de la anarquía o Shades of Blue, junto a Jennifer Lopez, una trayectoria constante pero siempre desde un segundo plano. Hollywood nunca volvió a ofrecerle un personaje capaz de igualar el impacto de aquel que la convirtió en una estrella. Dos décadas después su nombre vuelve a ser noticia, aunque por razones muy distintas a las que un día parecían augurarle una larga carrera en la cima de la televisión.

World.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ consigue el mejor día de estreno en la historia de España
World.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day, la última entrega del famoso superhéroe de Marvel, recaudó 3,2 millones de euros este miércoles en su primer día de proyección en las salas españolas. La cifra convierte el debut en la mejor jornada de estreno de la historia del cine en España, según los datos facilitados por la auditora Rentrak. En solo 24 horas, la película casi alcanza lo recaudado el primer fin de semana por los títulos más taquilleros del año en el mercado nacional: La odisea, de Christopher Nolan (4,4 millones de euros), y Super Mario Bros (4,9 millones). También roza ya la mitad de lo cosechado en sus primeros tres días por Torrente presidente (6,9 millones), el gran éxito de la temporada.

La cinta, protagonizada una vez más por Tom Holland y distribuida por Sony Pictures, ha desembarcado en 421 cines y más de un millar de pantallas de todo el país, lo que supone uno de los mayores despliegues comerciales registrados hasta la fecha en la industria española. La película aspira a un estreno de miércoles a domingo superior a los 10 millones de euros y a firmar uno de los mejores debuts a nivel mundial del año.

Con los datos, sigue la estela trazada por su predecesora, Spider-Man: No Way Home, que en 2021 cosechó siete millones de euros en el mercado español durante su primer fin de semana. En la taquilla norteamericana —en el cine, la taquilla no va por países sino por territorios, y en ese caso se agrupan EE UU y Canadá—, aquel título logró el segundo mejor estreno de la historia al recaudar 230,5 millones de euros (260 millones de dólares). Para esta nueva entrega, que estrenará el 31 de julio en el país norteamericano, la publicación especializada Variety sitúa las proyecciones de su primer fin de semana entre los 260 y los 280 millones de dólares en los más de 4.300 cines donde se exhibirá.

De confirmarse estos pronósticos, entraría en un club muy selecto: a lo largo de la historia del cine, solo nueve títulos han logrado superar la barrera de los 200 millones de dólares en su fin de semana de estreno en ese territorio. Una lista de éxitos que encabeza otro gigante de Marvel, Vengadores: Endgame (2019), con una apertura de 357 millones de dólares a nivel nacional y 1.200 millones de dólares en todo el mundo.

Dirigida por Destin Daniel Cretton —responsable de Shang-Chi y la leyenda de los Diez Anillos—, la nueva película del famoso superhéroe, la joya de la corona comercial para Marvel y Sony, apuesta por cuarta vez por Tom Holland en el papel de Peter Parker. Junto a él, un reparto coral reúne a habituales como Zendaya y Jacob Batalon con nombres como Jon Bernthal, Sadie Sink, Mark Ruffalo, Michael Mando y Tramell Tillman.

Se trata de un personaje tremendamente popular y multigeneracional. Lo contó Jorge Iván, codirector del festival Celsius 232 y las Jornadas del Cómic de Avilés a EL PAIS hace unos días: “Spiderman ha sabido adaptarse a cada generación sin perder su esencia. En los últimos años, el gran acierto ha sido Miles Morales, nacido en el universo Ultimatey consolidado definitivamente con las películas de Spider-Verse. Su éxito radica en que plantea tramas complejas y, al mismo tiempo, respeta tanto a los aficionados veteranos como a las nuevas generaciones”.

World.title: La UEFA y sus federaciones nacionales acuerdan boicotear las competiciones de la FIFA por querer privatizar el Mundial
World.content:
Gianni Infantino, presidente de la FIFA, y Aleksander Ceferin, presidente de la UEFA, durante la 50.ª reunión del Congreso Ordinario de la UEFA en Bruselas , el 12 de febrero de 2026

El organismo rector del fútbol europeo toma la decisión de negar la participación de las selecciones en los Mundiales por unanimidad hasta que Infantino deje sin efecto su propuesta de privatizar la Copa del Mundo

La UEFA y sus 55 asociaciones nacionales han acordado por unanimidad no participar en las competiciones de la FIFA, tras la reunión convocada ayer de urgencia. El órgano de gobierno del fútbol europeo, presidido por Alexander Ceferin, respondió con el boicot a la propuesta del presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, que el martes pasado presentó un proyecto para vender una participación de la Copa del Mundo a inversores particulares seleccionados por una empresa muy próxima a la familia de Donald Trump, el presidente de Estados Unidos.

El choque entre la unión de federaciones de Europa y la unión mundial de federaciones, dos organizaciones sin ánimo de lucro domiciliadas en Suiza que regulan y administran gran parte de los beneficios del juego más popular del planeta, alcanza su punto culminante. La medida adoptada ayer amenaza con una fractura sin precedentes en la historia de un campeonato masculino que desde 1930 fue conquistado por Europa en 13 de sus 22 ediciones y su homólogo femenino en cuatro de nueve, siendo la actual campeona España, que defendería el año que viene el título en Brasil. De profundizarse el conflicto, las consecuencias adquieren repercusiones impensables. Por ejemplo, que las selecciones de España y Portugal no participen en la próxima Copa del Mundo, prevista para 2030, principalmente, en estadios de España, Portugal y Marruecos. Que ayer Infantino se encontrara en Rabat para asistir a la celebración del 27 aniversario del ascenso al trono del rey Mohamed VI parece todo menos una coincidencia.

“La UEFA y sus asociaciones nacionales no participarán en competiciones de la FIFA”, rezó el comunicado oficial. “La UEFA y sus 55 asociaciones se plantan como uno solo. Por unanimidad y de manera inequívoca rechazamos la propuesta de la FIFA de transferir la propiedad del Mundial y de otras competiciones de la FIFA a inversores privados”.

“Ninguna de las 55 selecciones nacionales de la UEFA participará en las competiciones de la FIFA mientras estas propuestas permanezcan en pie”, concluyó el texto, “a menos que estas propuestas sean abandonadas en su totalidad y se presenten garantías de que la FIFA nunca más abrirá su gobernanza o sus competiciones a la propiedad privada”.

El martes pasado Infantino presentó un proyecto que incluía la creación de una empresa subsidiaria que acogería los derechos del Mundial previa venta de una participación por valor de 4.000 millones de dólares a inversores privados. Estos inversores serían seleccionados por Thrive Capital, empresa propiedad de Joshua Kushner, hermano de Jared Kushner, el yerno de Trump.

Infantino propuso a las 221 federaciones nacionales que integran la FIFA que aceptaran el plan y a cambio les prometió multiplicar la financiación. El presidente de la FIFA, que hace alarde de su amistad con Trump, repitió que creía en los procesos “democráticos”. Pero exigió velocidad. El miércoles, presentó un ultimátum a las 211 federaciones nacionales. Si antes del 19 de septiembre respondían afirmativamente, recibirían 40 millones de dólares cada una; si se negaban, la financiación se les quedaría en 2,7 millones de dólares, un 75% menos.

“Intimidación”

El comunicado de la UEFA criticó el chantaje. “Las asociaciones nacionales de todo el mundo han sido abordadas con un ultimátum”, dice el escrito; “o aceptan la captura irreversible de la mayor competición del fútbol o aceptan las consecuencias. Esto no es una decisión democrática [en el original, entre comillas] es gobernar mediante la intimidación. Un acto de coerción impropio de una institución encargada de velar por el fútbol mundial”.

“Es irresponsable e indefendible”, apunta, “que una propuesta tan significativa haya sido concebida en secreto y sacada a la luz de repente sin ningún procedimiento comprensible de consultas con los actores encargados de velar por el juego. No se trata solo de un profundo fallo de liderazgo, sino de la abdicación del deber de la FIFA de custodiar el fútbol mundial”.

La UEFA y la CONCACAF, la organización de asociaciones de fútbol de Norteamérica, Centroamérica y el Caribe, se han opuesto más o menos frontalmente a Infantino. Nada se sabe, sin embargo, de la CONMEBOL, la organización de Sudamérica, que no se ha pronunciado, ni tampoco de la confederación de África, que se ha limitado a decir que “estudiará” la oferta. Gobiernos y federaciones de Francia, Reino Unido e Italia se han manifestado en contra del plan privatizador. Otro tanto ocurrió este martes en la Comisión Europea, en donde el comisario de Juventud, Cultura y Deporte, Glenn Micallef, se opuso enérgicamente a la privatización del Mundial e incluso advirtió que estudiaría medidas legales para exigir responsabilidades a la FIFA.

Las manifestaciones en Europa contrastan con el silencio ibérico. Ni el Gobierno español ni la Federación, organizadores del Mundial 2030, se han pronunciado. Este periódico ha contactado con la oficina del presidente de la Federación, Rafael Louzán, sin obtener respuesta. Solo Javier Tebas, presidente de la Liga, y ejecutivo de UEFA, se ha pronunciado vehementemente contra la empresa de Infantino.

World.title: El lento declive de La Sexta
World.content:
Artículos estrictamente de opinión que responden al estilo propio del autor. Estos textos de opinión han de basarse en datos verificados y ser respetuosos con las personas aunque se critiquen sus actos. Todas las columnas de opinión de personas ajenas a la Redacción de EL PAÍS llevarán, tras la última línea, un pie de autor —por conocido que éste sea— donde se indique el cargo, título, militancia política (en su caso) u ocupación principal, o la que esté o estuvo relacionada con el tema abordado

El verano es tiempo de programas que no requieran mucha atención y series de relleno, aunque las plataformas hayan cambiado algo la cosa. También de poner nota a la temporada. ¿Quién nos iba a decir hace apenas un lustro que Telecinco sería de nuevo la gran perdedora y que Antena 3 encadenaría ese mismo espacio de tiempo arrollando a sus seguidores? Mientras los de Mediaset seguían aferrados a los chismes de Cantora, que cada vez importan menos y lo que sorprende es que todavía importen algo, y a un ecosistema de tentadores, tronistas y exconcursantes de realities a los que aparean y/o enfrentan en favor del share, Antena 3 y su contenido familiar les adelantaron por la derecha. Y ya ni siquiera siente a Telecinco como rival; ese honor le corresponde a una TVE reforzada en todas sus líneas que, gracias al Mundial, termina el mes como líder indiscutible.

¿Quién nos iba a decir también que la lucha más emocionante iba a ser la de las hermanas menores? Con una Cuatro tan potente que ha llegado a sobrepasar a Telecinco gracias a una columna vertebral sustentada por Nacho Abad, Risto Mejide e Iker Jiménez, a los que no me dirán que no les vendrían pintiparados Pedrerol y su Chiringuito para completar el póker del desparrame mediático. Un auge tan impredecible como el declive de La Sexta. La cadena que nació joven y audaz, la cara progresista de Atresmedia, se desangra en audiencia a pesar de mantener intacta su estructura y su capacidad para responder en el acto a cualquier acontecimiento.

Pase lo que pase, ahí estará Ferreras contándoselo, aunque eso implique acortar sus vacaciones, como acaba de hacer para informar sobre los incendios. A pesar de su incuestionable entrega, su programa es el espacio que más ha sufrido el desgaste; del 15% en el que se movía hace cinco años, Al rojo vivo ha caído a menos de la mitad y ve cómo es superado a diario no solo por TVE, también por En boca de todos, y esto es para hacérselo mirar. Es difícil saber si la causa es la veleidad de los espectadores, encandilados por las novedades de otras cadenas, o si, como le siguen recordando muchos en redes sociales, aquel diálogo con Villarejo en el que aceptaba dar una información “muy burda” contra Podemos fue suficiente para erosionar la imagen progresista de toda la cadena. Una cadena en la que están Iñaki López, Wyoming y Marc Giró. Lo que cuesta ganar credibilidad y lo fácilmente que se pierde.

World.title: Los críticos se ríen de la obra artística de Adrien Brody: perros con bandana, pollo frito y un mural a lo Warhol
World.content:
El actor neoyorquino lleva dos años centrado en la creación de grandes ‘collages’. En las subastas se venden por miles de dólares, pero para las redes y la crítica especializada siguen siendo motivo de burla

Ni profundos personajes como en El pianista, ni apabullantes decorados como en El Brutalista, el último trabajo de Adrien Brody está lleno de perritos con bandanas y souvenirs baratos de Nueva York. Hace unas semanas, el doble ganador del Oscar a mejor actor anunciaba su inesperada colaboración con Raising Cane’s, cadena estadounidense de comida rápida especializada en pollo frito. El motivo era el tercer aniversario de uno de los restaurantes situado en Times Square y, para celebrarlo, Brody diseñó un gran mural publicitario en el que mezclaba imágenes del fundador, Todd Graves, y su perro, con grafitis y referencias a su propia carrera.

“Compuesta por fragmentos de carteles y otros restos urbanos desgastados que he ido recopilando por toda la ciudad de Nueva York, junto con el programa de mano de mi debut en Broadway, The fear of 13, la pieza evoca la dureza, la perseverancia y el espíritu emprendedor que definen la trayectoria de Graves, el espíritu de Nueva York y esa estética urbana con la que siempre me he sentido identificado”, explicaba el propio Brody en un comunicado oficial. Sin embargo, esta sucesión de hipérboles no terminó de convencer a la crítica especializada ni a las redes, que enseguida se lanzaron a despedazarlo.

El actor debutó en el mundo arte con la exposición 'Hot Dogs, Hamburgers, and Handguns' en la Art Basel de Miami de 2015. Gustavo Caballero (Getty Images)

En X, un usuario tildaba la obra de “arte de mierda de perro”, mientras que, en la revista ARTnews, el crítico Alex Greenberger se refería al collage como “la última monstruosidad artística” de Brody. Pero esta reacción no es en absoluto novedosa. El actor y productor neoyorquino lleva más de una década compaginando su carrera en el cine con su faceta como artista plástico y, aunque sus collages —inspirados en grandes del arte contemporáneo como Andy Warhol o Jean-Michel Basquiat— se han llegado a vender en subastas por cientos de miles de dólares, no han dejado nunca de ser motivo de mofa.

“Cuando empecé me sorprendían estas reacciones, pero ya no. Ahora entiendo esa necesidad del público de encasillarlo todo”, reflexionaba Brody en la revista Interview, fundada en su día por el propio Warhol, sobre el rechazo que despertaba su incursión en el mundo del arte. “Pero la gente creativa necesita distintos canales para expresarse, ¿no? Además yo descubrí esta pasión mucho antes que la interpretación”, añadía. En la misma entrevista, revelaba que su padre, Elliot Brody, profesor de instituto y pintor aficionado durante toda su vida, le había inculcado la pasión por el arte. En cambio, su madre, Sylvia Plachy —mítica fotógrafa de la revista semanal The Village Voice— le enseñó a sentirse cómodo delante de las cámaras.

Lucy Liu firmando una de las caricaturas del elenco de 'God Of Carnage' hechas por ella en 2010. Eugene Gologursky (Getty Images)

De hecho, de adolescente, Brody intentó estudiar arte en la reputada escuela Fiorello H. LaGuardia. No lo aceptaron, pero le recomendaron matricularse en la rama de interpretación del mismo centro. Allí se decidió su destino. Hasta 2015, cuando el actor, con 42 años y una carrera más que consolidada en el cine, debutó por todo lo alto en el mundo arte con la exposición Hot Dogs, Hamburgers, and Handguns en la Art Basel de Miami, la feria de arte contemporáneo más prestigiosa de América. La muestra giraba en torno a tres elementos típicamente estadounidenses —los perritos calientes, las hamburguesas y las pistolas— y ya entonces desplegaba esa mezcla de manidas referencias al arte pop y la cultura urbana que tanto enfurece hoy al público.

Entonces, sin embargo, pasó más desapercibida. Algunas revistas como Newsweek se preguntaban si hubiera llegado hasta allí sin su fama, pero, al fin y al cabo, no era el primer actor, ni iba a ser el último, que probara suerte en el arte. Dentro de esa lista de estrellas entregadas a los lienzos se extiende un amplio espectro: desde las mejor valoradas, como Lucy Liu, que expone desde los años noventa y hoy se considera más artista que actriz; Jim Carrey, que casi llegó a convertirse en un viñetista político; o Viggo Mortensen, hasta las más vilipendiadas como el siempre polémico James Franco, Sylvester Stallone o Johnny Depp, cuyos retratos de amigos famosos parecen recién salidos de los primeros programas de edición fotográfica. Pero, en general, ninguno llega a trascender de los círculos más cerrados.

Castle Fine Art, en Windsor, exhibe obras de la colección debut de Johnny Depp, 'Friends & Heroes'. Geoffrey Swaine (Avalon / Contacto)

Una decepción brutal

La inquina que despierta la obra de Brody nació el año pasado con su última gran película: El Brutalista. Después de la larga campaña de promoción de la película, Brody volvió a ganar el Oscar dejando momentos tan comentados como un interminable discurso, que muchos compararon con las tres horas y media de duración de la cinta, o el chicle que tiró a las manos de su mujer justo antes de empezar hablar. Apenas dos meses después de ese momento de máximo escrutinio, el actor inauguró Made in America, su primera gran exposición en años, en la galería Eden de Nueva York y la crítica fue demoledora.

En los lienzos de gran tamaño daba rienda a las mismas fijaciones de siempre, grafiteando y degradando a conciencia iconos que iban desde Mickey Mouse y Maggie Simpson hasta Marilyn Monroe, el escudo de Ferrari, Jean-Michel Basquiat e incluso él mismo. La exposición también dedicaba un espacio a las ratas de Nueva York, con las que el artista aseguraba haberse sentido siempre muy identificado, y a una mesa llena de chicles, para que los visitantes los mascaran y los pegasen en un lienzo vacío. El impulso de la exposición le llevó a vender una de las piezas dedicadas a Monroe en una subasta celebrada en Cannes por unos 425.000 dólares, que actualmente equivalen a unos 372.000 euros. El precio desorbitado consiguió que en las redes sociales corriesen ríos de memes sobre el actor y sus obras.

Brody inauguró 'Made in America', su primera gran exposición en años, en 2025 en la galería Eden de Nueva York. Darla Khazei (Reuters)

En el portal Artnet, la crítica de arte Annie Armstrong acuñó el término “red-chip art” para describir la popularización de este tipo de arte de colores estridentes, estilo cartoon y trazas de grafiti. La expresión es un juego de palabras con el concepto de “blue-chip”, utilizado en el mundo de los coleccionistas para referirse a las obras de esos artistas de renombre, como Picasso, Van Gogh o Monet, que se consideran un valor seguro porque su precio suele mantenerse o aumentar con el tiempo. En contraposición, Armstrong utilizaba el término “red-chip” para referirse a ese tipo de artistas, a sus juicio sobrevalorados, que deben su éxito a un nuevo perfil de coleccionista: hombres que conducen un Cybertruck de Tesla, invierten en criptomonedas y escuchan el podcast del cómico ultraconservador Joe Rogan.

Adrien Brody posa con Radioman en la inauguración de su exposición 'Made in America'. Darla Khazei/INSTARimages via Re

“La única diferencia apreciable entre Brody y cualquier artista red-chip del montón es la insistencia que tiene por incorporar su propio rostro en las obras”, escribía. “Resulta desconcertante ver a un artista tan exitoso en un medio desenvolverse con tanta torpeza en otro”. Sin embargo, la crítica más demoledora que el actor ha recibido hasta la fecha llegó de la mano de Claire Bishop, profesora de historia del arte en el centro CUNY, en las páginas del diario The New York Times.

“Decir que parecen imágenes generadas por inteligencia artificial a partir de las búsquedas “grafiti del Lower East Side de los años noventa”, “Americana” y “nostalgia Disney” sería incluso demasiado generoso. En realidad, se asemejan al tipo de arte urbano descafeinado que se vende en la calle 53, a las puertas del MoMA, o en las aceras del SoHo: obras dirigidas a turistas que buscan un recuerdo de Nueva York con apariencia artística, pero sin ningún desafío estético”, zanjaba Bishop.

World.title: One person dies, six injured in crash between lorry and minibus
World.content:
One person has died and six others have been seriously injured in a head-on collision between a minibus and a lorry in Overijssel.

The crash happened on the N48 near Balkbrug, around 20km east of Zwolle, at around 11.30am on Thursday. All the victims were sitting in the minibus, which had Belgian numberplates.

Fire appliances, ambulances and an air ambulance were called to the crash site. Six passengers were taken to different hospitals in the area, while the seventh was pronounced dead at the scene. The lorry driver was unharmed.

The road is likely to be closed for several hours while police carry out investigations and the road is cleared of debris.

World.title: University launches ethics probe into Red Bull professor’s work
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Utrecht University has begun an investigation into its pharmacology department after a professor was accused of not declaring payments for research from companies, including energy drinks manufacturer Red Bull.

Joris Verster published several papers on energy drinks and alcohol in his capacity as associate professor, without disclosing that he was also paid as a consultant for Red Bull and US-based Sen-Jam Pharmaceuticals.

The university does not prohibit consultancy work, but academics are required to disclose any relevant secondary activities when they publish papers under conflict of interest rules.

The investigation follows reports in several Dutch and international media outlets, including Trouw, De Groene Amsterdammer and Investico, that Verster’s research was published without any reference to his paid work for Red Bull and Sen-Jam.

Verster set up a private company, NeuroClinics, for his consultancy work, which frequently overlapped with his academic research.

Hangover pill

He carried out a study into a hangover pill produced by Sen-Jam which concluded, based on a questionnaire circulated around his students, that the medicine did not encourage people to consume more alcohol.

Mariëtte van den Hoven, professor of medical ethics at Amsterdam’s UMC medical centre, said Verster’s methods amounted to a conflict of interest “by using the university to promote your personal goals.”

Another study, published in 2010, concluded that drinking a can of Red Bull improved driving performance, based on observing drivers for four hours in a simulator. It was publicised under the heading “Can Red Bull fuel better driving?”

Verster also published research that disputed claims that mixing energy drinks with alcohol were damaging to people’s health and could lead to aggressive behaviour or unsafe sexual practices.

His conclusion was that combining the drinks meant users consumed less alcohol and were less prone to reckless behaviour.

Sick leave

Verster himself, who has been on sick leave since the start of May, told Trouw he had always been transparent about his private work.

“I have been a consultant for many companies and stated it in all my papers, even when it concerned a minor role,” he said. “I informed Utrecht University about my work as a consultant and the university approved it.”

World.title: Eighth species of American crayfish found in Dutch rivers
World.content:
A new species of crayfish has been found in Dutch rivers, the eighth type to establish itself in the Netherlands after being introduced in the upper Rhine.

The calico crayfish (Faxonius immunis), originally from North America, was spotted in Gelderland by ecologist Pim Lemmers, who first encountered the creatures in a nature reserve near Karlsruhe decades ago.

“I’d been expecting them and looking out for them for a while,” he told NOS. “Last year I found a crayfish pincer and I knew straight away that it might be a significant one.“

The discovery of the pincer, together with the results of DNA samples, are enough to confirm that the crayfish have made it to the Dutch river system.

The water authority in Rivierland has reported the presence of the crayfish to the food standards regulator NVWA, which will in turn notify the European Union, and triggered the protocol for dealing with invasive exotic species.

The Dutch agriculture ministry has set up a working group to investigate how the crayfish can be prevented from spreading. Crayfish damage the local environment by eating indigenous plants and animals and digging in river banks.

“We’re at a very uncertain stage, because are they just in the Klompenwaard area of the Rhine or are they already in our regional waters? Can we keep them out of the waters?” said José Vos, senior policy adviser for the water board.

World.title: Post-Covid fatigue not just caused by inactivity, study finds
World.content:
Patients with post-Covid syndrome suffer muscle damage that cannot be fully be explained by inactivity, research led by scientists at Amsterdam’s Vrije Universiteit (VU) has found.

The team compared the blood and muscle tissue of patients with long Covid and chronic fatigue (ME) with a group of healthy people who spent 60 days in bed as part of a study simulating the effects of space travel.

The post-Covid and ME patients had suffered from energy dips that caused them to avoid exercising or spend long periods in bed, which has a degrading impact on the skeletal muscles.

But the researchers, led by Rob Wüst, a movement scientist at the VU, found differences in the colour of the muscle fibres between the two groups, indicating that the post-Covid patients had a much lower oxygen capacity.

“As skeletal muscle characteristics differ between patients and healthy individuals after bed rest, physical inactivity cannot solely explain the lower exercise capacity and skeletal muscle adaptations in long Covid and ME/CFS patients,” they wrote in a paper published in Nature Communications.

The healthy individuals from the space programme still had bright red fibres, which are still oxygen-rich, while the patients had white fibres, which become exhausted much faster.

Rapid tiredness

The researchers said the difference could explain why post-Covid and ME sufferers become tired so quickly even after modest levels of exercise or exertion. “The redder the fibres, the more stamina a person has,” Wüst explained.

Lung specialist Merel Hellemons, of the Erasmus MC teaching hospital in Rotterdam, told the Volkskrant that the findings were a crucial development in understanding how to treat patients with conditions such as post-Covid syndrome.

“Many patients hear that they need to move more or that being less active is bad for them,” she said.

Wüst said patients should still be encouraged to be more mobile to avoid damage to their muscles, skeletons and cardiovascular system caused by inactivity. “The question is: what is possible? We need more tailored solutions,” he said.

Dutch airline KLM booked a higher-than-expected profit in the first half of the year, despite the rise in fuel prices caused by ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

The company reported revenue of €6.9 bn in the six months to June, an 8% increase compared to the same period last year.

The airline benefited from a decrease in flights from competitors like Qatar Airways and Emirates because of the unrest in the region.

“The measures we are implementing are having a positive impact on our results,” CEO Marjan Rintel said in a statement.

Those measures included passing on higher fuel prices to customers, particularly on long-haul flights.

Yesterday, the Air France-KLM airline group announced they had put in an offer for a stake in Portugal’s TAP airline. Lisbon said last year that it was seeking a major international airline to buy most of the 49.9 percent stake that it planned to sell.

German airline Lufthansa also submitted a bid.

World.title: Man who strangled partner jailed after new forensic method used
World.content:
A man has been convicted of attempting to kill his partner in the first case to use new techniques to detect signs of strangulation in domestic violence.

The 33-year-old man from Rozenburg grabbed the woman by the neck as an argument turned violent last November. Police were alerted by neighbours and pulled the man away from his victim, who later said she was “turning blue”.

She was examined by a medical specialist using a new procedure developed in Rotterdam to gather forensic evidence faster in suspected cases of strangulation.

The doctor said the attack could have been fatal if it was prolonged, a detail that allowed prosecutors to argue that the attack should be classed as attempted manslaughter.

The procedure was introduced last December to try to detect strangulation, which is seen as an early warning sign of femicide, in domestic abuse investigations before the victim’s injuries heal and the evidence disappears.

200 referrals

The medical agency FARR, based in Rotterdam, anticipated receiving 200 inquiries a year, but was called on 150 times in the first three months. In 92% of cases doctors concluded the injuries could have been caused by strangulation. Nine in 10 victims were female and 78% of inquiries were related to domestic violence.

“It’s a huge number,” the agency’s managing director Geranda Zeelenberg told NOS. “Previously we hardly ever saw these people. They were probably always there, but the research we’ve begun has increased awareness of these cases.”

The man from Rozenburg was sentenced to 360 days in prison for attempted manslaughter, including 169 days suspended, and a community service order of 150 hours, in line with the prosecution’s demands.

His lawyer told the court he had no recollection of the events on the night of the attack because he had been taking alcohol and amphetamines, but argued that he had attacked her to try to force her to have sex rather than attempting to kill her.

World.title: Middle East conflict adds to pressure to fill Dutch gas reserves
World.content:
The Netherlands is lagging behind its European partners in filling its gas reserves for the winter, just as a key supplier in the Middle East has announced further restrictions on supplies caused by the conflict between the US and Iran.

QatarEnergy extended “force majeure” restrictions on its LNG cargoes until the end of September, affecting a total of 24 cargoes to European customers.

The company signed a contract to supply up to 3.5 million tonnes of liquified gas to the Netherlands per annum, which came into force this year, but the invocation of force majeure has put this commitment in jeopardy.

The Netherlands’ gas reserves are currently at 36.6% capacity, well below the EU average of 56%.

Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which triggered a spike in prices, the EU set a target of reaching 90% capacity by November 1. Since then European nations have had to find alternatives to Russian gas.

The Netherlands achieved this level for the first three years, but in 2025 it peaked at just 74% and at the start of April this year the four Dutch storage facilities were at less than 5% capacity.

Energy minister Stientje van Veldhoven said last month she was “confident” that the gas reserves would be filled for the winter, but admitted that the government needed to be “vigilant”.

Demand for gas has also increased during the summer as more consumer and businesses install air conditioning, putting more pressure on energy.

The Dutch government also has agreements to buy gas from Norway and the United States, or could resort to the open market.

The wholesale price of gas on the TTF market, operated by Gasunie, has risen by 50% since mid-June as a result of ongoing attacks by Iran and the US on facilities in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Thieves walked off with all of the chairs from the Bonnefanten Museum café in Maastricht in the early hours of Monday.

Café manager Freek Joosten told local news network L1 that camera footage showed the perpetrators making several trips carrying stacks of chairs at around 4am.

The designer seats are valued at more than €21,000.

The chairs were tied down with iron cables and the grounds are monitored by multiple cameras. The museum has reported the theft to the police.

The museum, which sits on Avenue Céramique in the Limburg capital, specialises in visual arts.

The terrace was recently renovated and the chairs were from designer Fermob Luxembourg. The thieves also took a waste container.

Visitors are still welcome in the café. Joosten has temporarily reallocated the chairs from his catering business to use on the terrace.

Police have asked anyone who saw anything unusual in the vicinity on the night of July 26 to 27, or who may have camera footage, to contact them.

World.title: Poland appoints new official to promote country’s brand internationally
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, a professor at Wrocław University of Economics, noted that her appointment signals “a shift” from simple promotional activities to “managing the reputation of our great country”. The move comes as Poland seeks to capitalise on its economic success, including growth in tourism and continued investments. But the government says that current promotion efforts lack a single strategy and are fragmented. Czas na markę Polska! Witamy na pokładzie prof. Barbarę Mróz – Gorgoń 🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/PPX2eWTRSm — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 29, 2026 Last year, Poland’s sport and tourism ministry appointed Mróz-Gorgoń, who also advises companies and institutions on branding strategy and founded a think tank dedicated to promoting Poland, to an interministerial team tasked with developing a comprehensive new branding strategy for Poland. The government said, however, that efforts to promote Poland were so far fragmented and lacked a single strategy, which is why it created the post of commissioner for promotion of the Poland brand. As the first specialist to take the position, Mróz-Gorgoń will be tasked with preparing a strategy to build a national brand and help implement it, coordinate activities to help grow tourism, support investments, and improve Poland’s position on the world stage. “We will create one programme resulting in the joint promotion of our country’s brand,” said Tusk. According to the government, this will come at no further cost, but ensure that existing funds will be spent in a more “coherent and effective way”. Mróz-Gorgoń, meanwhile, noted that “the Poland brand is not the property of the government. It is created by entrepreneurs, artists, athletes, local governments and millions of Poles at home and abroad”. Developing this brand “means more investment, recognition of our brands and products abroad, and it also provides greater strength in international relations,” she continued. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP annually within a decade, from about 5% now, and for Poland to become a leader in the sector in central and eastern Europe. Foreign direct investment in Poland grew from just under 15.5 billion zloty in 2003, a year before the country joined the European Union, to around 61.3 billion zloty last year, according to figures from the National Bank of Poland (NBP). Various state and private companies – such as delivery giant InPost, insurer PZU, and train manufacturer Pesa – are establishing themselves abroad by buying some of their rivals. The international success of some Polish athletes – including football player Robert Lewandowski and tennis star Iga Świątek – has also helped Poland improve its international recognition.
